title_zh: 【可跳过·非课程内容】复习计划与今天的安排
title_en: [Skippable · not course material] Revision plans and today's arrangement

points.zh: 学生问老师是不是每次课前都会重看之前的录像，学生自己还没来得及，但打算这么做。
points.en: The student asks whether the teacher rewatches the earlier recordings each time; the student has not yet done so but intends to.

points.zh: 学生说手上的复习材料和课上讲的内容对不上，感觉两边不是一套东西。
points.en: The student says his own revision material does not line up with what is taught in class; the two do not feel like the same body of content.

points.zh: 老师解释他为什么一直不建议现在就往前复习：今天讲的脂质代谢和糖酵解那一章串得非常紧。
points.en: The teacher explains why he has not pushed for reviewing earlier chapters yet: today's lipid metabolism is tightly interlocked with the glycolysis chapter.

points.zh: 他说脂质代谢讲着讲着就会遇到糖代谢和三羧酸循环的知识点，两边会自然串起来。
points.en: He says that while teaching lipid metabolism one keeps running into sugar-metabolism and TCA-cycle content; the two link up on their own.

points.zh: 他的计划是：先把全部代谢途径讲完，把这些基础的知识学完。
points.en: His plan is to first finish teaching all the metabolic pathways, i.e. get the basic material covered.

points.zh: 然后再单独做一次大复习，把不同的代谢途径串到一起。
points.en: Only then will he run a separate big review session that ties the different pathways together.

points.zh: 学生同意这个安排，双方确认后直接进入正课。
points.en: The student agrees to this arrangement, and after confirming they go straight into the lecture proper.

extra.zh: 把不同代谢「串起来」，实际上只需要串几个交汇分子：G6P（糖的分岔口，通向糖酵解、PPP、糖原）、丙酮酸、乙酰CoA（糖、脂、生酮氨基酸共同的汇合点）、草酰乙酸（TCA 的门槛，也是糖异生的起点）、α-酮戊二酸（转氨反应的接口）。记住这五个分子各自有几条进出口，整合复习就有骨架了。
extra.en: Tying the pathways together really means tying together a handful of junction molecules: G6P (the branch point into glycolysis, PPP and glycogen), pyruvate, acetyl-CoA (where sugar, fat and ketogenic amino acids converge), oxaloacetate (the gate of the TCA cycle and the start of gluconeogenesis) and alpha-ketoglutarate (the transamination interface). Knowing the inputs and outputs of these five gives the integrated review its skeleton.

extra.zh: 本讲是整个代谢部分的最后一讲：先补完糖代谢剩下的分支（磷酸戊糖途径、糖异生、糖原），再讲脂质的分解与合成，最后开一个氨基酸代谢的头。
extra.en: This is the last lecture of the metabolism block: it first finishes the remaining branches of carbohydrate metabolism (pentose phosphate pathway, gluconeogenesis, glycogen), then covers lipid catabolism and synthesis, and finally opens amino acid metabolism.

extra.zh: 复习材料和课堂对不上是常态，原因是编排逻辑不同：教材按分子类别分章（糖一章、脂一章、蛋白一章），课堂按途径与区室讲。对着途径图记（谁在胞质、谁在基质、谁连着谁）比对着章节目录记有效得多。
extra.en: A mismatch between textbook and lecture is normal because they are organised differently: textbooks split by molecule class (one chapter each for carbohydrate, lipid, protein), while the lecture runs by pathway and compartment. Revising from a pathway map (what is cytosolic, what is in the matrix, what feeds what) works far better than revising from a table of contents.

quiz.q_zh: 老师为什么主张先把所有代谢途径讲完、最后再统一复习？
quiz.q_en: Why does the teacher want to finish all the metabolic pathways first and only then run a combined review?

options.zh: 脂质代谢会不断串到糖酵解和三羧酸循环
options.en: Lipid metabolism keeps running into glycolysis and TCA

options.zh: 复习材料的章节顺序和课堂顺序完全一致
options.en: The revision material's chapters match the lecture order

options.zh: 考试只考最后一次大复习里出现的内容
options.en: The exam tests only what the final review session covers

options.zh: 每条代谢途径彼此独立，可以分开单独背诵
options.en: Each metabolic pathway stands alone and is learned apart

quiz.explain_zh: 他给的理由就是脂质代谢讲着讲着就会遇到糖代谢和 TCA 的知识点。说「章节顺序完全一致」正好相反，学生抱怨的就是对不上；「只考大复习内容」是课上没有的说法；「彼此独立」与他整堂课强调的交汇点矛盾。
quiz.explain_en: His stated reason is that teaching lipid metabolism keeps colliding with sugar metabolism and the TCA cycle. The claim that chapter order matches is the opposite of the student's complaint; the claim about the exam is never made; and treating pathways as independent contradicts the junction points he stresses all lecture.

quiz.q_zh: 学生在这段对话里提出的困扰是什么？
quiz.q_en: What problem does the student raise in this exchange?

options.zh: 脂质代谢的教材章节还没有拿到手
options.en: He has not yet obtained the lipid metabolism chapter

options.zh: 手上的复习材料和课上讲的内容对不上
options.en: His revision material does not match what is taught

options.zh: 上次课留的作业题目做不出答案
options.en: He cannot solve the problems set in the last class

options.zh: 课程录像没有字幕所以完全听不懂
options.en: The recordings have no subtitles so he cannot follow

quiz.explain_zh: 学生说的是「我现在的复习材料感觉没有讲的你讲的」，即材料和课堂内容对不上。字幕、教材没拿到、作业做不出这三件事在这段对话里都没有出现。
quiz.explain_en: The student says his revision material does not correspond to what is being taught. Subtitles, a missing textbook chapter and unsolved homework are none of them mentioned in this exchange.

title_zh: 今天的内容与整个代谢章的重要性排序
title_en: Today's contents and the importance ranking across the metabolism block

points.zh: 糖的代谢还剩一个「小尾巴」——磷酸戊糖途径等分支途径，今天先把它带过。
points.en: Carbohydrate metabolism has one loose end left, the pentose phosphate pathway and other side branches, which he will run through quickly today.

points.zh: 他明说这一小块的重要性远远低于 EMP（糖酵解）和三羧酸循环，但仍有作用，所以不能完全跳过。
points.en: He says outright that this piece matters far less than EMP (glycolysis) and the TCA cycle, but it still has a role, so it cannot be skipped entirely.

points.zh: 今天最重要的是脂质代谢；此外学生上次提到想学蛋白质代谢。
points.en: The most important item today is lipid metabolism; in addition, the student had asked earlier about protein metabolism.

points.zh: 蛋白质代谢里最重要的是尿素循环 urea cycle，他会看今天能不能讲到。
points.en: Within protein metabolism the key item is the urea cycle, which he will reach if time allows.

points.zh: 脂质代谢的难度比 TCA 循环低很多，但小知识点一个接一个，属于「次重点」。
points.en: Lipid metabolism is much less difficult than the TCA cycle, but it consists of many small facts one after another, so it counts as a secondary priority.

points.zh: 整个代谢大章里最重要的是糖代谢，糖代谢里又以 EMP 途径和 TCA 途径为重中之重。
points.en: Across the whole metabolism block, carbohydrate metabolism is the most important, and within it the EMP pathway and the TCA cycle are the core of the core.

points.zh: 其次重要的是脂质代谢，而脂质里分解代谢比合成代谢更重要——这与他在代谢开篇讲过的总原则一致：分解代谢往往比合成代谢更重要。
points.en: Lipid metabolism ranks next, and within it catabolism outweighs anabolism, consistent with the general rule he stated when metabolism began: catabolic pathways usually matter more than anabolic ones.

points.zh: 代谢部分还剩蛋白质代谢和核酸代谢两章，蛋白质代谢又比核酸代谢重要，所以越往后讲重要性越低。
points.en: Two chapters remain, protein metabolism and nucleic acid metabolism; protein outweighs nucleic acid, so importance keeps declining toward the end.

extra.zh: 为什么分解代谢考得更多：分解途径在各类生物中高度保守、步骤固定、有一本清清楚楚的能量账（每步产几个 NADH、几个 ATP），题目好出也好判；合成途径分支多、组织特异性强（肝、脂肪、乳腺各不相同），并且受激素层层调控，很难压成一道有唯一答案的题。
extra.en: Why catabolism is examined more: catabolic pathways are highly conserved, have a fixed step order and a clean energy ledger (how many NADH and ATP per step), which makes them easy to ask and to mark. Anabolic pathways branch, are tissue-specific (liver, adipose, lactating mammary gland all differ) and are layered with hormonal control, which makes a single-answer question hard to write.

extra.zh: 尿素循环之所以是蛋白代谢的核心考点：共 5 步，跨线粒体基质（氨甲酰磷酸合成酶 I、鸟氨酸氨甲酰转移酶）和胞质（精氨基琥珀酸合成酶、裂解酶、精氨酸酶）两个区室，并且通过延胡索酸与天冬氨酸和 TCA 循环直接相连（aspartate–argininosuccinate shunt）。它是「区室 + 与其他途径接口」的典型题材。
extra.en: The urea cycle is the core exam topic of protein metabolism because it has five steps split across two compartments, the mitochondrial matrix (CPS I, ornithine transcarbamylase) and the cytosol (argininosuccinate synthetase, argininosuccinate lyase, arginase), and because it connects directly to the TCA cycle through fumarate and aspartate, the aspartate-argininosuccinate shunt. It is the classic 'compartments plus interfaces' question.

extra.zh: 「分解代谢比合成代谢重要」不等于「合成就是分解倒过来跑」。本课后面反复出现的正是反例：糖酵解 10 步，糖异生要用 4 个不同的酶绕过其中 3 步；β-氧化在线粒体基质、用 CoA 和 FAD/NAD⁺，脂肪酸合成在胞质、用 ACP 和 NADPH。方向相反的两条路几乎总是不同的酶、不同的区室。
extra.en: 'Catabolism matters more' does not mean 'anabolism is catabolism run backwards'. The counterexamples come up repeatedly later in this lecture: glycolysis has ten steps, and gluconeogenesis needs four different enzymes to bypass three of them; beta-oxidation runs in the mitochondrial matrix on CoA with FAD/NAD+, while fatty acid synthesis runs in the cytosol on ACP with NADPH. Opposing routes almost always use different enzymes in different compartments.

quiz.q_zh: 按老师给出的排序，整个代谢大章里重要性最高的是哪一块？
quiz.q_en: By the teacher's ranking, which block matters most in the whole metabolism chapter?

options.zh: 糖代谢，尤其是糖酵解和三羧酸循环
options.en: Carbohydrate metabolism, above all EMP and the TCA

options.zh: 脂质代谢，尤其是脂肪酸从头合成
options.en: Lipid metabolism, above all de novo fatty acids

options.zh: 蛋白质代谢，尤其是尿素循环一段
options.en: Protein metabolism, above all the urea cycle part

options.zh: 核酸代谢，尤其是嘌呤的从头合成途径
options.en: Nucleic acid metabolism, above all de novo purines

quiz.explain_zh: 他的原话是糖代谢最重要，糖代谢里 EMP 和 TCA 是「重中之重」。脂质排第二、蛋白质排第三、核酸排最后；尿素循环确实是蛋白质代谢里最重要的一段，但蛋白质代谢整体排在糖和脂之后。
quiz.explain_en: He states that carbohydrate metabolism is the most important and that EMP and TCA are the core of the core within it. Lipid ranks second, protein third and nucleic acid last; the urea cycle is indeed the key part of protein metabolism, but protein metabolism as a whole sits behind carbohydrate and lipid.

quiz.q_zh: 他对脂质代谢内部的重要性是怎么排的？
quiz.q_en: How does he rank importance within lipid metabolism itself?

options.zh: 分解代谢比合成代谢更重要
options.en: Catabolism is the more important of the two halves

options.zh: 合成代谢比分解代谢更值得先看
options.en: Anabolism deserves attention ahead of catabolism

options.zh: 只有酮体生成那一段需要掌握
options.en: Only the ketone body section needs to be mastered

options.zh: 两者重要性相同，不必分主次
options.en: Both matter equally, so no priority is needed here

quiz.explain_zh: 他把代谢开篇讲过的总原则套到脂质上：分解代谢比合成代谢更重要。他没有说合成优先，没有把内容缩到只剩酮体，也没有说两者不分主次。
quiz.explain_en: He applies the general rule stated at the start of the metabolism block to lipids: catabolism outweighs anabolism. He does not put synthesis first, does not reduce the topic to ketone bodies, and does not call the two equally weighted.

quiz.q_zh: 他点名蛋白质代谢里最重要的内容是什么？
quiz.q_en: Which item does he name as the most important within protein metabolism?

options.zh: 尿素循环从氨到尿素的全过程
options.en: The urea cycle from ammonia through to urea itself

options.zh: 一碳单位与四氢叶酸的转移反应
options.en: One-carbon units and tetrahydrofolate transfer steps

options.zh: 转氨基作用的机制与磷酸吡哆醛
options.en: The transamination mechanism and pyridoxal phosphate

options.zh: 支链氨基酸在肌肉中的分解途径
options.en: Branched-chain amino acid breakdown inside muscle

quiz.explain_zh: 他说「蛋白质的代谢里边最重要的就是尿素循环 urea cycle」，并说看今天能不能讲到。转氨基、支链氨基酸、一碳单位都属于氨基酸代谢的其他内容，这一段没有点名。
quiz.explain_en: He says the most important part of protein metabolism is the urea cycle and hopes to reach it today. Transamination, branched-chain amino acid breakdown and one-carbon transfer all belong to other parts of amino acid metabolism and are not singled out here.

title_zh: 各代谢途径的区室定位，以及 PPP 作为 EMP 的旁支
title_en: Where each pathway runs, and PPP as a side branch of EMP

points.zh: 磷酸戊糖途径在有些课本里写作 PPP 途径；老师坦言不确定三个 P 各代表什么，只说看到 PPP 就知道是磷酸戊糖途径。
points.en: The pentose phosphate pathway is written PPP in some textbooks; he admits he is not sure what each P stands for and only says that PPP means the pentose phosphate pathway.

points.zh: PPP 主要存在于细胞的胞浆，也就是细胞质里。
points.en: PPP runs mainly in the cytoplasm, i.e. the cytosol.

points.zh: 他强调对每一条代谢途径的发生部位都要有清晰认知，能区分出每种途径主要在哪个部位就够了。
points.en: He stresses that one must have a clear picture of where every pathway runs; being able to place each pathway in its compartment is enough.

points.zh: EMP 途径（糖酵解）100% 在细胞质、细胞浆里发生。
points.en: The EMP pathway (glycolysis) runs 100% in the cytosol.

points.zh: 理由是几乎所有生物都能用糖酵解产能，而有的生物根本没有线粒体。
points.en: The reason is that essentially all organisms can use glycolysis to make energy, and some organisms have no mitochondria at all.

points.zh: TCA 循环 90% 以上的步骤在线粒体内膜内侧（基质）里发生。
points.en: Over 90% of the TCA cycle's steps occur inside the inner mitochondrial membrane, i.e. in the matrix.

points.zh: 他说有几个步骤例外：电子传递链 complex II 那一步，以及丙酮酸形成乙酰CoA 那一步，都发生在线粒体内膜上，理由是它们的蛋白是膜蛋白。
points.en: He names exceptions: the electron transport chain's complex II step and the step converting pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, both said to occur on the inner membrane because their proteins are membrane proteins.

points.zh: PPP 可以理解成 EMP 途径的补充、一条旁支、一条分路，但与糖酵解挨得非常近。
points.en: PPP can be understood as a supplement to EMP, a side branch or bypass that sits very close to glycolysis.

points.zh: PPP 的起点是 G6P（六磷酸葡萄糖）；学生答 G6P 是糖酵解第二步的产物，老师纠正为第一步。
points.en: PPP starts from G6P (glucose-6-phosphate); the student answers that G6P is the product of glycolysis step two and the teacher corrects this to step one.

extra.zh: 他说丙酮酸→乙酰CoA 那一步在线粒体内膜上、因为「它的蛋白是一个膜蛋白」。这句话把两件事捆在了一起：complex II（琥珀酸脱氢酶）确实是内膜整合蛋白，这半句没问题；但丙酮酸脱氢酶复合体（PDH）是线粒体基质里的可溶性多酶复合体，那一步在基质中发生。（严格说 PDH 与内膜有松散结合，但教学上一律按基质记。）
extra.en: He says the pyruvate to acetyl-CoA step happens on the inner membrane because 'its protein is a membrane protein'. That fuses two separate facts: complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) really is an integral inner-membrane protein, and that half is fine; but the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is a soluble multi-enzyme complex of the mitochondrial matrix, and that step occurs in the matrix. (PDH is loosely associated with the inner membrane, but for exam purposes always record it as matrix.)

extra.zh: PPP 就是 pentose phosphate pathway 三个词的首字母，老师没查到的答案就是这个；旧教材里它还叫 HMP shunt（hexose monophosphate shunt，己糖单磷酸支路），中文有时写「磷酸己糖旁路」，指的是同一条途径。
extra.en: PPP is simply the initials of pentose phosphate pathway, which is the answer he could not recall. Older texts call it the HMP shunt (hexose monophosphate shunt); the Chinese name 磷酸己糖旁路 refers to the same pathway.

extra.zh: 「PPP 在细胞质」是对的，但活性在组织之间差别极大：肝、脂肪组织、肾上腺皮质、哺乳期乳腺、睾丸（都要大量 NADPH 做还原性合成）和红细胞（要 NADPH 维持谷胱甘肽）活跃；骨骼肌几乎不跑 PPP。这就是为什么 G6PD 缺乏首先表现为溶血，而不是肌无力。
extra.en: 'PPP is cytosolic' is right, but its activity varies enormously between tissues: liver, adipose, adrenal cortex, lactating mammary gland and testis (all needing NADPH for reductive synthesis) and red cells (needing NADPH to keep glutathione reduced) are highly active, while skeletal muscle runs almost none. That is why G6PD deficiency presents as haemolysis rather than muscle weakness.

extra.zh: 他说判断代谢部位「主要也就是核糖体和细胞质，你区分出来就 OK 了」。要对比的两个区室是线粒体（基质／内膜）和细胞质，核糖体是蛋白质合成的场所，与糖脂代谢的区室划分无关；他紧接着讲的正是「糖酵解在细胞质、TCA 在线粒体」，所以这里指的应该是线粒体。（也可能是转写把「线粒体」整词替换成了「核糖体」。）
extra.en: He says that placing a pathway 'mainly comes down to telling the ribosome and the cytosol apart'. The two compartments to contrast are the mitochondrion (matrix / inner membrane) and the cytosol; the ribosome is the site of protein synthesis and has nothing to do with the compartmentation of sugar and lipid metabolism. What he says immediately afterwards, glycolysis in the cytosol and TCA in the mitochondrion, shows he means mitochondrion. (It may also be a whole-word transcription substitution.)

quiz.q_zh: 关于 PPP、EMP 和 TCA 的发生部位，哪一组是正确的？
quiz.q_en: Which set correctly places PPP, EMP and the TCA cycle?

options.zh: PPP 在细胞质，EMP 在基质，TCA 在胞质
options.en: PPP in cytosol, EMP in matrix, TCA back in cytosol

options.zh: PPP 在基质，EMP 在细胞质，TCA 在内膜
options.en: PPP in matrix, EMP in cytosol, TCA on inner membrane

options.zh: PPP 在内质网，EMP 在细胞质，TCA 在基质
options.en: PPP in the ER, EMP in cytosol, TCA in the matrix

options.zh: PPP 在细胞质，EMP 在细胞质，TCA 主要在基质
options.en: PPP in cytosol, EMP in cytosol, TCA mainly in matrix

quiz.explain_zh: PPP 和糖酵解都在胞浆，TCA 90% 以上在线粒体基质。把 PPP 放进基质或内质网都错；把糖酵解放进线粒体更错——糖酵解在没有线粒体的生物里照样进行。
quiz.explain_en: Both PPP and glycolysis are cytosolic, and over 90% of the TCA cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix. Placing PPP in the matrix or the ER is wrong, and placing glycolysis in the mitochondrion is worse, since glycolysis runs in organisms that have no mitochondria at all.

quiz.q_zh: 丙酮酸脱氢酶复合体催化的丙酮酸→乙酰CoA 这一步，实际发生在哪里？
quiz.q_en: Where does the pyruvate dehydrogenase step, pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, actually take place?

options.zh: 线粒体外膜上，面向胞质一侧起作用
options.en: On the outer membrane, acting on the cytosolic face

options.zh: 细胞质中，产物再运进线粒体基质里
options.en: In the cytosol, the product then entering the matrix

options.zh: 线粒体内膜上，因为它是一个整合膜蛋白
options.en: On the inner membrane, as an integral membrane protein

options.zh: 线粒体基质中，它是可溶性多酶复合体
options.en: In the mitochondrial matrix, a soluble enzyme complex

quiz.explain_zh: 课上把这一步和 complex II 捆在一起说成内膜膜蛋白。complex II（琥珀酸脱氢酶）确实是内膜整合蛋白，但 PDH 是基质里的可溶性多酶复合体；它既不在外膜，也不在胞质——丙酮酸是先经载体进入基质后才被氧化脱羧的。
quiz.explain_en: In class this step was bundled with complex II and called a membrane protein. Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) genuinely is an integral inner-membrane protein, but PDH is a soluble matrix complex. It is neither on the outer membrane nor in the cytosol: pyruvate is carried into the matrix first and oxidatively decarboxylated there.

quiz.q_zh: 他给出的「糖酵解 100% 在细胞质」的理由是什么？
quiz.q_en: What reason does he give for glycolysis running 100% in the cytosol?

options.zh: 因为细胞质的 pH 比线粒体基质低得多
options.en: Because cytosolic pH is far lower than in the matrix

options.zh: 因为葡萄糖无法通过线粒体外膜的孔道
options.en: Because glucose cannot cross the outer-membrane porins

options.zh: 因为糖酵解的酶都需要线粒体膜作支架
options.en: Because glycolytic enzymes need a membrane scaffold

options.zh: 因为很多生物根本没有线粒体这个结构
options.en: Because many organisms have no mitochondrion at all

quiz.explain_zh: 他的论证是：糖酵解基本上是所有生物都能用来产能的途径，而有的生物连线粒体都没有，所以它只能在胞质里跑。需要线粒体膜作支架、pH 更低、外膜孔道挡住葡萄糖这三条都不是他给的理由，也都与事实不符（外膜的 porin 对小分子通透）。
quiz.explain_en: His argument is that glycolysis is the energy-yielding route available to essentially all organisms, some of which have no mitochondria, so it must run in the cytosol. Needing a membrane scaffold, a lower pH and glucose being blocked at the outer membrane are none of them his reason, and none is true either (outer-membrane porins are permeable to small molecules).

title_zh: G6P 为什么被锁在细胞里，以及 PPP 的总路线
title_en: Why G6P is trapped inside the cell, and the overall route of PPP

points.zh: 葡萄糖是水溶性非常高的分子，人的细胞表面又有很多葡萄糖转运蛋白。
points.en: Glucose is a highly water-soluble molecule, and human cell surfaces carry many glucose transporters.

points.zh: 所以葡萄糖理论上可以比较自由地进出细胞。
points.en: Glucose can therefore in principle move in and out of cells fairly freely.

points.zh: 一旦给它上一个磷酸，这个分子就带上了负电荷，不再被葡萄糖转运蛋白识别。
points.en: Once a phosphate is added, the molecule carries a negative charge and is no longer recognised by the glucose transporters.

points.zh: 葡萄糖进入胞浆后由己糖激酶加上磷酸变成 G6P，就被锁定在细胞质里了。
points.en: After entering the cytosol, glucose is phosphorylated by hexokinase to G6P and is thereby locked inside the cell.

points.zh: 被锁住之后它就很容易被各种途径利用，因此 G6P 是很多途径的共同分子、一个汇合点。
points.en: Being trapped, it is readily used by many pathways, which makes G6P a shared molecule and a convergence point.

points.zh: 他举的例子是：EMP 途径有 G6P，现在学的 PPP 也是从 G6P 开始的。
points.en: His example: EMP has G6P, and the PPP now being taught also starts from G6P.

points.zh: PPP 的主线是 G6P 经一系列分子重排变成 5-磷酸核酮糖，即 5 位磷酸化的核酮糖，一个五碳糖。
points.en: The main line of PPP is G6P rearranging into ribulose-5-phosphate, a five-carbon sugar phosphorylated at position 5.

points.zh: 再经过一些重排变成 F6P（6-磷酸果糖），F6P 最后又回到 G6P 的形式，所以 PPP 以 G6P 开始、以 G6P 结束。
points.en: Further rearrangements give F6P (fructose-6-phosphate), which returns to G6P, so PPP both begins and ends at G6P.

points.zh: 最大的区别在数目：开始是六分子 G6P，最后变成五分子 G6P，中间「插出来」的那一分子葡萄糖相当于被降解掉，全部给了 NADPH。
points.en: The difference is in the count: six molecules of G6P go in and five come out, and the one glucose that drops out is in effect degraded, all of it going into NADPH.

extra.zh: G6P 作为「汇合点」具体有四个去向：进糖酵解（磷酸葡萄糖异构酶→F6P）、进 PPP（G6PD）、进糖原合成（磷酸葡萄糖变位酶→G1P→UDP-葡萄糖）、以及在肝和肾由葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶水解成游离葡萄糖送出细胞。记住这四条出口，「枢纽」才不是一句空话。
extra.en: G6P as a hub has four concrete fates: into glycolysis (phosphoglucose isomerase to F6P), into PPP (G6PD), into glycogen synthesis (phosphoglucomutase to G1P and then UDP-glucose), and in liver and kidney hydrolysis by glucose-6-phosphatase to free glucose for export. Those four exits are what 'hub' actually means.

extra.zh: 「磷酸化就被锁死在细胞里」有一个重要例外，而这个例外正是下一节糖异生的关键：肝、肾和肠上皮细胞含有葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶，能把 G6P 水解回葡萄糖释放入血。肌肉没有这个酶，所以肌糖原分解出来的葡萄糖只能自己用，不能升血糖。
extra.en: 'Phosphorylation locks it in' has one crucial exception, and it is exactly the key to the gluconeogenesis section that follows: liver, kidney and intestinal epithelium have glucose-6-phosphatase and can hydrolyse G6P back to glucose for release into blood. Muscle lacks the enzyme, so glucose from muscle glycogen can only be used locally and never raises blood glucose.

extra.zh: 6 G6P → 5 G6P 的完整配平式是：6 G6P + 12 NADP⁺ + 6 H₂O → 5 G6P + 6 CO₂ + 12 NADPH + 12 H⁺ + Pi。也就是每分子 G6P 在氧化阶段产 2 个 NADPH、放 1 个 CO₂，六分子就是 12 NADPH 和 6 CO₂。
extra.en: The full balanced equation for 6 G6P to 5 G6P is: 6 G6P + 12 NADP+ + 6 H2O gives 5 G6P + 6 CO2 + 12 NADPH + 12 H+ + Pi. In other words each G6P yields 2 NADPH and releases 1 CO2 in the oxidative phase, so six molecules give 12 NADPH and 6 CO2.

extra.zh: 己糖激酶 hexokinase 与葡萄糖激酶 glucokinase 的分工是常考点：肌肉等组织的 hexokinase Km 低（约 0.1 mM）、易饱和、受产物 G6P 反馈抑制；肝和胰岛 β 细胞的 glucokinase Km 高（约 10 mM）、不被 G6P 抑制，所以只有餐后血糖升高时肝脏才大量摄取葡萄糖。
extra.en: The division of labour between hexokinase and glucokinase is a standard exam point: hexokinase in muscle and elsewhere has a low Km (about 0.1 mM), saturates readily and is feedback-inhibited by its product G6P; glucokinase in liver and pancreatic beta cells has a high Km (about 10 mM) and is not inhibited by G6P, so the liver takes up glucose in bulk only when blood glucose rises after a meal.

quiz.q_zh: 葡萄糖一进细胞就被磷酸化成 G6P，最直接的后果是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the most immediate consequence of glucose being phosphorylated to G6P on entry?

options.zh: 分子量增大以后无法通过细胞膜上的水通道蛋白扩散出去
options.en: The larger mass stops it diffusing out via aquaporin pores

options.zh: 变成还原糖之后可以被己糖激酶再次识别并继续磷酸化
options.en: It becomes a reducing sugar hexokinase phosphorylates again

options.zh: 溶解度下降后在细胞质里以颗粒的形式沉积下来储存
options.en: Its solubility drops so it deposits as granules for storage

options.zh: 带上负电荷后不再被葡萄糖转运蛋白识别，被留在胞内
options.en: Negative charge blocks transporter recognition, trapping it

quiz.explain_zh: 老师的逻辑正是：磷酸带负电，转运蛋白不再认它，G6P 就被锁在胞质里供各条途径使用。葡萄糖本来就不走水通道蛋白；G6P 不会被己糖激酶再磷酸化（反而反馈抑制它）；G6P 高度水溶，不会沉积成颗粒——沉积成颗粒的是糖原。
quiz.explain_en: His logic is exactly that the phosphate's negative charge makes the transporters stop recognising the molecule, so G6P stays in the cytosol for the various pathways. Glucose does not use aquaporins; G6P is not phosphorylated again by hexokinase but feedback-inhibits it; and G6P is highly soluble and does not form granules, which is what glycogen does.

quiz.q_zh: PPP 的碳骨架总路线是下面哪一条？
quiz.q_en: Which of these is the overall carbon route of PPP?

options.zh: G6P → 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸 → 乳酸 → G6P
options.en: G6P to 6-phosphogluconate to lactate and back to G6P

options.zh: G6P → 1-磷酸葡萄糖 → UDPG → G6P
options.en: G6P to glucose-1-phosphate to UDP-glucose and to G6P

options.zh: G6P → 5-磷酸核酮糖 → F6P → 回到 G6P
options.en: G6P to ribulose-5-phosphate to F6P and back to G6P

options.zh: G6P → 1,6-二磷酸果糖 → 丙酮酸 → G6P
options.en: G6P to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate to pyruvate to G6P

quiz.explain_zh: 老师画的就是这条环：G6P 经重排到五碳的 5-磷酸核酮糖，再重排回 F6P，F6P 回到 G6P。经 1,6-二磷酸果糖到丙酮酸是糖酵解；6-磷酸葡萄糖酸确实是 PPP 的中间物，但它不通向乳酸；经 1-磷酸葡萄糖和 UDPG 的是糖原合成。
quiz.explain_en: This is the loop he draws: G6P rearranges to the five-carbon ribulose-5-phosphate, then back to F6P and on to G6P. The route through fructose-1,6-bisphosphate to pyruvate is glycolysis; 6-phosphogluconate is indeed a PPP intermediate but does not lead to lactate; and the route through glucose-1-phosphate and UDP-glucose is glycogen synthesis.

quiz.q_zh: 6 G6P → 5 G6P 这个式子里「消失」的那一分子葡萄糖去了哪里？
quiz.q_en: In the equation 6 G6P to 5 G6P, where does the one 'missing' glucose go?

options.zh: 以六个 CO₂ 脱羧丢掉，还原力交给 NADP⁺
options.en: Lost as six CO2 by decarboxylation, reducing power to NADP+

options.zh: 以六个甘油醛的形式留在胞质，还原力交给谷胱甘肽
options.en: Left in cytosol as six glyceraldehydes, power to glutathione

options.zh: 以六个乳酸的形式排到细胞外，还原力都交给 NAD⁺
options.en: Out as six lactates, with the reducing power going to NAD+

options.zh: 以六个乙酰CoA 进入 TCA，还原力交给 FAD
options.en: Into the TCA cycle as six acetyl-CoA, reducing power to FAD

quiz.explain_zh: 六分子 G6P 各脱羧丢一个碳，共放出 6 个 CO₂，同时把还原当量交给 NADP⁺ 生成 12 个 NADPH——这就是老师说的「相当于被降解了、全部给了 NADPH」。PPP 不产乳酸、不产乙酰CoA，也不直接把电子交给谷胱甘肽（是 NADPH 再经谷胱甘肽还原酶去还原 GSSG）。
quiz.explain_en: Each of the six G6P loses one carbon by decarboxylation, releasing 6 CO2 while passing reducing equivalents to NADP+ to make 12 NADPH, which is what he means by 'degraded and all of it given to NADPH'. PPP makes no lactate and no acetyl-CoA, and it does not hand electrons straight to glutathione; NADPH does that later via glutathione reductase.

title_zh: 丢掉的碳去哪了，这个反应式该记到什么程度
title_en: Where the lost carbon goes, and how much of the equation to memorise

points.zh: 老师反复强调 6 G6P → 5 G6P 只是为了把方程两边配平而写出的形式，不代表真正的物理过程。
points.en: He repeatedly stresses that 6 G6P to 5 G6P is written only to balance the equation and does not represent the real physical process.

points.zh: 他说 G6P 变成核酮糖的时候「就是少一个碳」，而「在后边它只是别的东西又给它加上了」。
points.en: He says that when G6P becomes ribulose it 'is simply one carbon short', and that 'later on something else just adds it back'.

points.zh: 他说每一分子葡萄糖在 G6P → 5-磷酸核酮糖 → F6P 的过程中都会给出氢离子，让 NADP 接受氢变成 NADPH。
points.en: He says each glucose gives up hydrogens along G6P to ribulose-5-phosphate to F6P, letting NADP accept them and become NADPH.

points.zh: 他找了一张 PPP 的图发给学生看，两人都评价「很复杂」。
points.en: He finds a PPP diagram and sends it to the student; both comment that it is very complicated.

points.zh: 他明确说这一节不需要记反应式，也不需要记每一步产生的能量，去记反而会干扰思路。
points.en: He states plainly that this section requires neither the equations nor the per-step energy yields, and that memorising them would only get in the way.

points.zh: 他说 PPP 的图不必看，只看他发的脂质代谢的图就可以，前面这部分真的不是很重要。
points.en: He says the PPP diagram need not be studied, only the lipid metabolism diagrams he sent, since this earlier material really is not very important.

points.zh: 书上之所以写这个反应式，是想说明整个 PPP 有两个作用。
points.en: The textbook writes the equation in order to convey that PPP serves two purposes.

points.zh: 作用之一：反应过程中产生五碳的核酮糖，而且并不是所有核酮糖都回到 G6P，有一部分以核糖的形式进入核酸的代谢。
points.en: One purpose: the pathway generates five-carbon ribulose, and not all of it returns to G6P; some enters nucleic acid metabolism in the form of ribose.

extra.zh: 「少一个碳，后边别的东西又给它加上了」是错的。那个碳是在 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸脱氢酶那一步以 CO₂ 脱羧丢掉的，一去不回。6 → 5 的配平不是靠把碳加回来，而是靠非氧化阶段的转酮酶 transketolase（搬二碳单位）和转醛酶 transaldolase（搬三碳单位）把六个五碳糖重排成五个六碳糖：C5×6 = C30 = C6×5。碳总数守恒，但没有任何一个碳「被加回原来那个位置」。
extra.en: 'One carbon short, and later something adds it back' is wrong. That carbon is lost as CO2 at the 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase step and never returns. The 6-to-5 balance comes not from adding carbon back but from the non-oxidative phase, where transketolase (moving two-carbon units) and transaldolase (moving three-carbon units) rearrange six pentoses into five hexoses: C5 x 6 = C30 = C6 x 5. Total carbon is conserved, but no carbon is ever restored to its original position.

extra.zh: 氧化阶段就三步酶，值得记住名字：葡萄糖-6-磷酸脱氢酶 G6PD（产 1 NADPH，是全途径的限速步，受 NADPH 反馈抑制）→ 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸内酯酶（只水解内酯环，不产 NADPH）→ 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸脱氢酶（产 1 NADPH，同时脱羧放 CO₂）。
extra.en: The oxidative phase is only three enzymes and the names are worth knowing: glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase G6PD (yields 1 NADPH, is the rate-limiting step of the whole pathway and is feedback-inhibited by NADPH), then 6-phosphogluconolactonase (merely hydrolyses the lactone ring, no NADPH), then 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (yields 1 NADPH while decarboxylating and releasing CO2).

extra.zh: 非氧化阶段的反应全部可逆，这正是 PPP 灵活的原因：细胞只要核糖不要 NADPH 时，可以由糖酵解的 F6P 和 3-磷酸甘油醛反向做出 5-磷酸核糖，完全绕开氧化阶段；只要 NADPH 不要核糖时，就把核酮糖全部转回 F6P 和 3-磷酸甘油醛送进糖酵解。
extra.en: Every reaction of the non-oxidative phase is reversible, which is what makes PPP flexible: when a cell needs ribose but not NADPH, it can build ribose-5-phosphate backwards from the glycolytic F6P and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate, bypassing the oxidative phase entirely; when it needs NADPH but not ribose, it converts all the ribulose back to F6P and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate and returns it to glycolysis.

extra.zh: 他全程把这几步叫「变构」（G6P 变构到核酮糖），指的是分子结构改变，不是酶学那一章的别构调节 allosteric regulation。做笔记时写「结构重排 / isomerisation」，不要写成 allosteric，否则会和 PFK-1、ACC 那类别构酶混成一团。
extra.en: Throughout he calls these steps 'bian gou' (G6P being 'restructured' into ribulose), meaning a change in molecular structure, not the allosteric regulation of the enzymology chapter. Write it up as structural rearrangement or isomerisation, never as allosteric, or it will blur into the genuinely allosteric enzymes such as PFK-1 and ACC.

quiz.q_zh: G6P 变成 5-磷酸核酮糖时少掉的那个碳，最终的去向是什么？
quiz.q_en: What ultimately happens to the carbon lost when G6P becomes ribulose-5-phosphate?

options.zh: 以 CO₂ 脱羧丢掉，不再被加回碳骨架
options.en: Lost as CO2 by decarboxylation and never re-added

options.zh: 由转酮酶从另一分子糖上重新补回到原位
options.en: Restored to place by transketolase from another sugar

options.zh: 转移到 CoA 上成为乙酰基进入 TCA
options.en: Moved onto CoA as an acetyl group entering the TCA

options.zh: 被羧化酶重新固定回到 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸上
options.en: Refixed onto 6-phosphogluconate by a carboxylase enzyme

quiz.explain_zh: 老师说「后边别的东西又给它加上了」，实际那个碳在 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸脱氢酶那一步以 CO₂ 离开，永远不回来。转酮酶确实存在，但它搬的是二碳单位、用于重排骨架，不是把丢掉的碳补回原位；PPP 不生成乙酰CoA；氧化阶段也没有把 CO₂ 再固定回去的羧化酶。
quiz.explain_en: He says 'something adds it back later', but in fact that carbon leaves as CO2 at the 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase step and never returns. Transketolase is real, but it moves two-carbon units to rearrange skeletons rather than restoring the lost carbon; PPP does not make acetyl-CoA; and there is no carboxylase refixing that CO2.

quiz.q_zh: 非氧化阶段把六个五碳糖变成五个六碳糖，靠的是什么？
quiz.q_en: What converts six pentoses into five hexoses in the non-oxidative phase?

options.zh: 羧化酶固定 CO₂、脱羧酶再释放 CO₂
options.en: A carboxylase fixing CO2, a decarboxylase releasing it

options.zh: 醛缩酶裂解六碳糖、异构酶再重新环化
options.en: Aldolase cleaving hexoses, isomerase cyclising them again

options.zh: 激酶加磷酸、磷酸酶再把磷酸都水解掉
options.en: A kinase adding phosphate, a phosphatase removing it all

options.zh: 转酮酶转二碳单位、转醛酶转三碳单位
options.en: Transketolase moving two- and transaldolase three-carbon

quiz.explain_zh: 转酮酶搬二碳单位、转醛酶搬三碳单位，把 C5×6 重排成 C6×5，碳总数守恒。羧化/脱羧会改变碳总数，与「重排」无关；醛缩酶属于糖酵解的裂解步骤；加磷酸再脱磷酸不改变碳骨架长度。
quiz.explain_en: Transketolase moves two-carbon units and transaldolase three-carbon units, rearranging C5 x 6 into C6 x 5 with total carbon conserved. Carboxylation and decarboxylation would change the carbon count, so they are not rearrangement; aldolase belongs to the cleavage step of glycolysis; and adding then removing phosphate changes no skeleton length at all.

title_zh: PPP 的另一项作用：NADPH 还原力，以及它究竟去哪里
title_en: The other job of PPP: NADPH as reducing power, and where it actually goes

points.zh: PPP 的另一项作用是把大量 NADP 还原成 NADPH，产出所谓的「还原力」。
points.en: The other job of PPP is to reduce large amounts of NADP to NADPH, producing what is called reducing power.

points.zh: 他说这个 NADPH 可以从细胞质经苹果酸-天冬氨酸穿梭，或者 3-磷酸甘油穿梭，重新回到线粒体内膜里去。
points.en: He says this NADPH can travel from the cytosol back into the mitochondrion via the malate-aspartate shuttle or the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle.

points.zh: 他说回到线粒体后再给出它的氢离子来产生能量。
points.en: He says that once inside the mitochondrion it gives up its hydrogens to generate energy.

points.zh: 紧接着他自己补充：PPP 产生的这个 NADPH 主要其实不是为了供能，并重复了一遍「主要不是为了供能」。
points.en: He immediately adds that the NADPH from PPP is mainly not for energy supply, repeating the point for emphasis.

points.zh: 他把 PPP 的作用归纳为两条：给出核酮糖、产生还原力。
points.en: He sums up PPP as two functions: supplying ribulose and producing reducing power.

points.zh: 他说 G6P 经三步酶变成 5-磷酸核酮糖，并且「每一步的变构过程中它其实都产生了 NADPH」。
points.en: He says G6P passes through three enzymatic steps to ribulose-5-phosphate, and that 'every one of those structural steps in fact produces NADPH'.

points.zh: 他把这几步称为氧化脱羧阶段，并说这部分不是很重要、反应式不需要记。
points.en: He calls these steps the oxidative decarboxylation phase and says it is not very important and that the equations need not be memorised.

points.zh: 他给出的记忆要求只有一句：G6P 变成 5-磷酸核酮糖的过程中会产生大量 NADPH，即大量还原力。
points.en: The only thing he asks the student to remember is one sentence: converting G6P to ribulose-5-phosphate produces a great deal of NADPH, i.e. reducing power.

points.zh: PPP 的意义他总结为：产生大量 NADPH，产生大量磷酸核糖，而磷酸核糖会掺入核酸的代谢。
points.en: He summarises the significance of PPP as producing plenty of NADPH and plenty of ribose phosphate, the latter feeding into nucleic acid metabolism.

extra.zh: 「NADPH 经苹果酸-天冬氨酸穿梭或 3-磷酸甘油穿梭回线粒体产能」这句是错的。这两条穿梭运的是胞浆 NADH 的还原当量，不是 NADPH。NADPH 不是氧化磷酸化的底物、不进呼吸链；它的去向是还原性生物合成（脂肪酸、胆固醇合成）和抗氧化防御（谷胱甘肽还原酶把 GSSG 还原成 GSH，过氧化氢酶体系）。他在约 12:45 处部分收回，说「PPP 产生的 NADPH 主要其实不是为了供能」，但「经穿梭回线粒体产能」这一句没有收回，做笔记时不要记这一句。
extra.en: 'NADPH returns to the mitochondrion on the malate-aspartate or glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle to make energy' is wrong. Those shuttles carry the reducing equivalents of cytosolic NADH, not NADPH. NADPH is not a substrate for oxidative phosphorylation and does not enter the respiratory chain; its destinations are reductive biosynthesis (fatty acids, cholesterol) and antioxidant defence (glutathione reductase regenerating GSH from GSSG, and the peroxide-handling systems). At around 12:45 he partly retracts this, saying the NADPH from PPP is mainly not for energy supply, but the sentence about shuttling back to the mitochondrion is never withdrawn, so do not record it.

extra.zh: 「每一步酶变都产生 NADPH」不对：氧化阶段三步里只有两步产 NADPH——G6PD 一分子、6-磷酸葡萄糖酸脱氢酶一分子（后者同时脱羧放 CO₂）；夹在中间的内酯酶只是水解内酯环，不产 NADPH。所以每分子 G6P 是 2 个 NADPH，不是 3 个。
extra.en: 'Every enzymatic step produces NADPH' is not right: of the three oxidative steps only two do, G6PD giving one NADPH and 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase giving another (while decarboxylating and releasing CO2); the lactonase in between merely hydrolyses the lactone ring and yields none. So each G6P gives 2 NADPH, not 3.

extra.zh: 细胞为什么要养 NAD 和 NADP 两套几乎一样的辅酶：NADP⁺ 只比 NAD⁺ 多一个 2′-磷酸，这个磷酸就是酶的识别标签。细胞把 NAD⁺/NADH 维持在高氧化态（胞质中约 700:1，利于分解代谢脱氢），把 NADPH/NADP⁺ 维持在高还原态（约 75:1，利于还原性合成）。两套分开，才能在同一个胞质里同时跑氧化和还原。
extra.en: Why the cell keeps two nearly identical coenzymes: NADP+ differs from NAD+ only by a 2'-phosphate, and that phosphate is the recognition tag enzymes read. The cell holds NAD+/NADH strongly oxidised (roughly 700:1 in the cytosol, favouring catabolic dehydrogenation) and NADPH/NADP+ strongly reduced (roughly 75:1, favouring reductive synthesis). Keeping the pools separate lets oxidation and reduction run simultaneously in the same cytosol.

extra.zh: G6PD 缺乏症是全世界最常见的酶缺陷，影响数亿人。红细胞没有线粒体，PPP 是它唯一的 NADPH 来源；NADPH 一断，谷胱甘肽还原酶补不上 GSH，红细胞抗不住氧化应激，在吃蚕豆、服用伯氨喹或磺胺类药、以及感染时发生急性溶血。这是「NADPH 用于抗氧化而非供能」最直接的临床证据。
extra.en: G6PD deficiency is the commonest enzyme defect in the world, affecting hundreds of millions of people. Red cells have no mitochondria, so PPP is their only source of NADPH; without it glutathione reductase cannot regenerate GSH, the cell cannot withstand oxidative stress, and acute haemolysis follows fava beans, primaquine or sulfonamides, or infection. This is the most direct clinical proof that NADPH serves antioxidant defence rather than ATP production.

quiz.q_zh: 磷酸戊糖途径产生的 NADPH，主要去向是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the main destination of the NADPH produced by the pentose phosphate pathway?

options.zh: 直接交给复合体 I 参与电子传递链的传递
options.en: Handed straight to complex I of the electron transport chain

options.zh: 经苹果酸-天冬氨酸穿梭进线粒体产 ATP
options.en: Into mitochondria on the malate-aspartate shuttle for ATP

options.zh: 经磷酸甘油穿梭交给 FAD 之后产 ATP
options.en: Onto FAD via the glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle to make ATP

options.zh: 用于还原性生物合成与谷胱甘肽抗氧化防御
options.en: Reductive biosynthesis and glutathione antioxidant defence

quiz.explain_zh: NADPH 是还原性合成（脂肪酸、胆固醇）和抗氧化（谷胱甘肽还原酶）的供氢体，不是氧化磷酸化的底物。两条穿梭运的是胞浆 NADH 的还原当量，与 NADPH 无关；复合体 I 特异识别 NADH，不接受 NADPH。老师在这一段说 NADPH 可以经穿梭回线粒体产能，随后自己补了一句「主要不是为了供能」。
quiz.explain_en: NADPH is the hydrogen donor for reductive synthesis (fatty acids, cholesterol) and antioxidant defence (glutathione reductase), not a substrate of oxidative phosphorylation. Both shuttles carry the reducing equivalents of cytosolic NADH and have nothing to do with NADPH, and complex I specifically recognises NADH and will not take NADPH. In this stretch he says NADPH can shuttle back for energy, then adds that it is mainly not for energy supply.

quiz.q_zh: 磷酸戊糖途径氧化阶段的三步酶反应中，产 NADPH 的情况是？
quiz.q_en: Among the three oxidative-phase enzyme steps of PPP, which produce NADPH?

options.zh: 三步全部都产，每分子 G6P 共 3 个 NADPH
options.en: All three do, giving 3 NADPH for every molecule of G6P

options.zh: 只有内酯酶那一步产，每分子共 1 个 NADPH
options.en: Only the lactonase step does, giving 1 NADPH per molecule

options.zh: 只有最后脱羧那一步产，每分子共 1 个 NADPH
options.en: Only the last decarboxylation does, giving 1 per molecule

options.zh: G6PD 与 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸脱氢酶这两步，共 2 个
options.en: G6PD and 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase, giving 2 in all

quiz.explain_zh: 课上说「每一步的变构过程中都产生了 NADPH」，实际只有两步：G6PD 产 1 个，6-磷酸葡萄糖酸脱氢酶产 1 个并脱羧放 CO₂。中间的 6-磷酸葡萄糖酸内酯酶只水解内酯环，不涉及氧化还原，所以每分子 G6P 是 2 个而不是 3 个或 1 个。
quiz.explain_en: In class he says every step of the rearrangement produces NADPH, but only two do: G6PD gives one, and 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase gives another while decarboxylating and releasing CO2. The intervening 6-phosphogluconolactonase only hydrolyses the lactone ring with no redox chemistry, so each G6P gives 2 rather than 3 or 1.

quiz.q_zh: 红细胞中 G6PD 缺乏为什么会在吃蚕豆或服药后引起溶血？
quiz.q_en: Why does G6PD deficiency in red cells cause haemolysis after fava beans or certain drugs?

options.zh: 红细胞唯一的 NADPH 来源断了，GSH 补不上
options.en: Their only NADPH source fails, so GSH is not regenerated

options.zh: 红细胞唯一的 ATP 来源断了，钠泵完全停止工作
options.en: Their only ATP source fails, so the sodium pump shuts down

options.zh: 红细胞唯一的 NADH 来源断了，乳酸就再也无法生成
options.en: Their only NADH source fails, so lactate can no longer form

options.zh: 红细胞唯一的核糖磷酸来源断了，膜蛋白无法再更新
options.en: Their only ribose source fails, so membrane turnover stops

quiz.explain_zh: 红细胞没有线粒体，PPP 是它唯一的 NADPH 来源，NADPH 又是谷胱甘肽还原酶把 GSSG 还原成 GSH 的供氢体；氧化应激一来就抗不住而溶血。红细胞的 ATP 来自糖酵解、NADH 来自 GAPDH 那一步，都不依赖 G6PD；成熟红细胞也不再合成膜蛋白。
quiz.explain_en: Red cells have no mitochondria, so PPP is their sole source of NADPH, and NADPH is the hydrogen donor glutathione reductase uses to turn GSSG back into GSH; without it oxidative stress bursts the cell. Red-cell ATP comes from glycolysis and their NADH from the GAPDH step, neither of which needs G6PD, and mature red cells no longer synthesise membrane protein.

title_zh: 糖异生登场：名字、「逆反应」的说法与三个能垒
title_en: Gluconeogenesis arrives: the name, the 'reverse reaction' claim, and three energy barriers

points.zh: 接下来学的是一条比较特殊的途径：糖异生，英文 gluconeogenesis。
points.en: The next pathway taught is a rather special one: gluconeogenesis.

points.zh: 他拆词根：neo 是「新的」的意思，直译过来就是「新的葡萄糖的再生」。
points.en: He parses the root: neo means new, so a literal reading is the new generation of glucose.

points.zh: 他一开始说糖异生「就是 TCA 循环——不是 TCA，是 EMP 循环，就是糖酵解的逆反应」。
points.en: He first says gluconeogenesis is 'the TCA cycle, no, the EMP cycle, i.e. the reverse of glycolysis'.

points.zh: 这条途径需要克服三个能量屏障（能垒）。
points.en: The pathway must overcome three energy barriers.

points.zh: 三个能垒对应 EMP 途径里三个正向不可逆的反应：葡萄糖→G6P（第一步不可逆，己糖激酶）；F6P→1,6-二磷酸果糖（第二步不可逆）；磷酸烯醇丙酮酸→丙酮酸（第三步不可逆）。
points.en: The three barriers correspond to the three irreversible forward reactions of EMP: glucose to G6P (the first, by hexokinase), F6P to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (the second), and phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate (the third).

points.zh: 糖异生是由「别的一些酶」来克服这三个不可逆反应的，所以在 EMP 途径里我们仍然认为这三步不可逆。
points.en: Gluconeogenesis uses a different set of enzymes to get past these three steps, so within EMP itself the three remain irreversible.

points.zh: 他强调：由那几个特定的酶催化的反应就是不可逆的，糖异生是另外几个酶构成的逆向路线。
points.en: He stresses that the reactions catalysed by those particular enzymes are irreversible, and that gluconeogenesis is a reverse route built from different enzymes.

points.zh: 他说细胞内可能 90% 的时间都在进行 EMP 途径，只有非常饥饿、血糖水平非常低的时候才发生糖异生。
points.en: He says cells may run EMP some 90% of the time, and that gluconeogenesis occurs only when one is very hungry and blood glucose is very low.

points.zh: 他说这三个反应式不需要看，因为都是 EMP 的逆反应，但还是决定大概过一遍。
points.en: He says the three equations need not be studied since they are just the reverse of EMP, but decides to go through them roughly anyway.

extra.zh: 开头那句「糖异生就是糖酵解的逆反应」（还把 EMP 说成「循环」，EMP 是途径不是循环）严格讲不成立：糖酵解十步中有七步的酶是可逆的、两条路共用，另外三步由完全不同的四个酶绕过——葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶、果糖-1,6-二磷酸酶、丙酮酸羧化酶 + PEP 羧激酶。他在约 15:30–16:00 自己补上了这一点（「糖异生是由别的一些酶来克服这三个不可逆反应的」），所以这只是开场表述不严谨，不是未纠正的错误。
extra.en: The opening claim that gluconeogenesis is simply the reverse of glycolysis (and calling EMP a cycle, when it is a pathway) does not hold strictly: seven of the ten glycolytic steps use reversible enzymes shared by both directions, while the other three are bypassed by four entirely different enzymes, glucose-6-phosphatase, fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, and pyruvate carboxylase plus PEP carboxykinase. He supplies this himself at roughly 15:30 to 16:00, so it is loose phrasing at the outset rather than an uncorrected error.

extra.zh: 「90% 的时间在走 EMP，只有非常饥饿才糖异生」说得过强。餐后吸收期一结束（进食后约 8–12 小时），肝糖原逐渐耗尽，糖异生就已经是肝脏产糖的主力，不需要「非常饥饿」；禁食 24 小时后肝脏输出的葡萄糖大部分来自糖异生。另外糖酵解和糖异生在同一个细胞里不会同时高速运行，由 F-2,6-BP 等互反调控避免底物空转，所以也谈不上「90% 的时间」。
extra.en: 'EMP 90% of the time, gluconeogenesis only when very hungry' is too strong. Once the post-absorptive state sets in (roughly 8 to 12 hours after eating) and liver glycogen runs down, gluconeogenesis is already the main source of hepatic glucose output, no extreme hunger required; after a 24-hour fast most hepatic glucose output is gluconeogenic. Moreover glycolysis and gluconeogenesis never run fast simultaneously in the same cell, being reciprocally regulated through fructose-2,6-bisphosphate to prevent futile cycling, so the '90% of the time' framing does not apply.

extra.zh: 三个不可逆步骤在糖酵解里的酶名要与糖异生的绕行酶配对记：己糖激酶 ↔ 葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶；磷酸果糖激酶 PFK-1 ↔ 果糖-1,6-二磷酸酶 FBPase-1；丙酮酸激酶 ↔ 丙酮酸羧化酶 + PEP 羧激酶。三对酶正好也是三个调控节点，F-2,6-BP 同时激活 PFK-1 和抑制 FBPase-1，是「两条路不会同时开」的开关。
extra.en: Learn the three irreversible glycolytic enzymes paired with their gluconeogenic bypasses: hexokinase against glucose-6-phosphatase; phosphofructokinase PFK-1 against fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase FBPase-1; pyruvate kinase against pyruvate carboxylase plus PEP carboxykinase. These three pairs are also the three regulatory nodes, and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate, which activates PFK-1 while inhibiting FBPase-1, is the switch that keeps the two routes from running at once.

extra.zh: 糖异生并不是全身细胞都能做：主要在肝脏（约 80–90%），其次是肾皮质，长期禁食时肾的贡献可上升到相当比例；小肠也有一定能力。肌肉没有葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶，因此永远不能向血液输出葡萄糖。
extra.en: Not every cell can perform gluconeogenesis: it is mainly hepatic (roughly 80 to 90%), with the renal cortex next and its share rising substantially in prolonged fasting, and the small intestine contributing some. Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase and therefore can never export glucose to the blood.

quiz.q_zh: 糖异生需要绕过的三个不可逆步骤，在糖酵解里分别由哪三个酶催化？
quiz.q_en: Which three glycolytic enzymes catalyse the irreversible steps that gluconeogenesis must bypass?

options.zh: 己糖激酶、磷酸果糖激酶、丙酮酸激酶
options.en: Hexokinase, phosphofructokinase and pyruvate kinase

options.zh: 己糖激酶、醛缩酶、3-磷酸甘油酸激酶
options.en: Hexokinase, aldolase and 3-phosphoglycerate kinase

options.zh: 葡萄糖激酶、烯醇化酶、苹果酸脱氢酶
options.en: Glucokinase, enolase and malate dehydrogenase enzyme

options.zh: 磷酸葡萄糖异构酶、醛缩酶、丙糖磷酸异构酶
options.en: Phosphoglucose isomerase, aldolase, triose isomerase

quiz.explain_zh: 三个能垒就是葡萄糖→G6P、F6P→1,6-二磷酸果糖、PEP→丙酮酸，分别由己糖激酶、磷酸果糖激酶、丙酮酸激酶催化。醛缩酶、3-磷酸甘油酸激酶、烯醇化酶、磷酸葡萄糖异构酶、丙糖磷酸异构酶催化的都是可逆步骤，两条路共用；苹果酸脱氢酶根本不在糖酵解主链上。
quiz.explain_en: The three barriers are glucose to G6P, F6P to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate and PEP to pyruvate, catalysed respectively by hexokinase, phosphofructokinase and pyruvate kinase. Aldolase, 3-phosphoglycerate kinase, enolase, phosphoglucose isomerase and triose phosphate isomerase all catalyse reversible steps shared by both directions, and malate dehydrogenase is not on the glycolytic main chain at all.

quiz.q_zh: 「糖异生就是糖酵解的逆反应」这个说法，严格讲应该怎么修正？
quiz.q_en: How should the claim 'gluconeogenesis is simply glycolysis run backwards' be corrected?

options.zh: 十步全部由同一批酶反向催化，方向由底物浓度决定
options.en: All ten steps reverse on the same enzymes by mass action

options.zh: 七步共用可逆的酶，三步不可逆步骤由另外的酶绕过
options.en: Seven steps share reversible enzymes, three are bypassed

options.zh: 两条途径没有任何共用的酶，是完全独立的两套系统
options.en: The two routes share no enzymes at all and stay separate

options.zh: 糖异生在线粒体里跑，糖酵解在胞质里跑，酶完全不同
options.en: Gluconeogenesis runs in mitochondria, glycolysis in cytosol

quiz.explain_zh: 十步中七步的酶可逆、两条路共用，三个不可逆步骤由四个不同的酶绕过（葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶、果糖-1,6-二磷酸酶、丙酮酸羧化酶、PEP 羧激酶）。说全部同一批酶忽略了三个能垒；说完全不共用酶忽略了那七步；糖异生除丙酮酸羧化酶那一步外主要在胞质进行，不是整条在线粒体。他自己在约 15:30 之后补上了正确说法。
quiz.explain_en: Seven of the ten steps use reversible enzymes shared by both directions, while the three irreversible ones are bypassed by four different enzymes: glucose-6-phosphatase, fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, pyruvate carboxylase and PEP carboxykinase. Saying the same enzymes do everything ignores the three barriers; saying no enzymes are shared ignores the seven; and apart from the pyruvate carboxylase step gluconeogenesis is largely cytosolic, not mitochondrial. He supplies the correct version himself after about 15:30.

title_zh: 绕过三个能垒：丙酮酸羧化酶、PEPCK、果糖二磷酸酶与葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶
title_en: Bypassing the three barriers: pyruvate carboxylase, PEPCK, FBPase and glucose-6-phosphatase

points.zh: 磷酸烯醇丙酮酸（PEP）→ 丙酮酸这一步，正方向由一个酶就能催化完成。
points.en: The forward step, phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate, is done by a single enzyme.

points.zh: 反过来则需要两个酶：先是丙酮酸羧化酶，给丙酮酸上一个羧基。
points.en: The reverse needs two enzymes: first pyruvate carboxylase, which adds a carboxyl group to pyruvate.

points.zh: 加上羧基后丙酮酸就变成草酰乙酸；他口述结构说「这里是个 COOH，这里是 CHR，这里又是 COOH」。
points.en: With that carboxyl added, pyruvate becomes oxaloacetate; he dictates the structure as 'a COOH here, a CHR here, and another COOH here'.

points.zh: 他先说第一步是在细胞质里用丙酮酸羧化酶给丙酮酸上羧基，草酰乙酸再经苹果酸-天冬氨酸穿梭进入线粒体。
points.en: He first says the first step happens in the cytosol, pyruvate carboxylase adding the carboxyl, with oxaloacetate then entering the mitochondrion on the malate-aspartate shuttle.

points.zh: 另一个酶叫磷酸烯醇丙酮酸羧激酶（PEPCK），他说这个酶名不用记。
points.en: The other enzyme is phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (PEPCK); he says the name need not be memorised.

points.zh: 他随即自我纠正：「我可能说反了，上面这步是在线粒体里边进行的，下边这个是在细胞浆」。
points.en: He then corrects himself: 'I may have said it backwards, the upper step happens in the mitochondrion and the lower one in the cytosol.'

points.zh: 这两步总共消耗两分子能量：一次 ATP、一次 GTP，用来克服 PEP→丙酮酸 的能量壁垒。
points.en: The two steps together cost two energy-carrying molecules, one ATP and one GTP, to overcome the PEP-to-pyruvate barrier.

points.zh: 另一处能垒：1,6-二磷酸果糖由果糖二磷酸酶变回 6-磷酸果糖，他说这一步不消耗能量，理由是正反应 F6P→1,6-二磷酸果糖 的 ΔG 稍微偏正、是吸能的，逆反应就是放能的。
points.en: Another barrier: fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is returned to F6P by fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, which he says costs no energy because the forward reaction has a slightly positive delta G and is endergonic, making the reverse exergonic.

points.zh: 还有一处能垒：G6P 变成葡萄糖这一步也不怎么耗能，而且只在特定细胞里发生——主要是储存糖原的地方，比如肝脏和少部分储存糖原的细胞。
points.en: The remaining barrier: converting G6P to glucose also costs little energy and occurs only in particular cells, chiefly the glycogen-storing tissues such as the liver and a few other cell types.

extra.zh: 他先把丙酮酸羧化酶说成在细胞质，随后（约 18:05）自己纠正为「上面这步在线粒体、下边在细胞浆」，以纠正后的版本为准：丙酮酸羧化酶在线粒体基质，需要生物素作辅基、消耗 ATP，并由乙酰CoA 别构激活；生成的草酰乙酸不能直接过内膜，要先还原成苹果酸（或转氨成天冬氨酸）出线粒体，在胞质再变回草酰乙酸，由 PEPCK 用 GTP 转成 PEP。
extra.en: He first places pyruvate carboxylase in the cytosol, then corrects himself at about 18:05 to 'the upper step in the mitochondrion, the lower in the cytosol'. Take the corrected version: pyruvate carboxylase sits in the mitochondrial matrix, uses biotin as its prosthetic group, consumes ATP and is allosterically activated by acetyl-CoA. The oxaloacetate it makes cannot cross the inner membrane directly, so it is reduced to malate (or transaminated to aspartate) for export, reconverted to oxaloacetate in the cytosol, and turned into PEP by PEPCK at the cost of GTP.

extra.zh: 他口述草酰乙酸结构为 COOH / CHR / COOH，漏掉了酮基碳。草酰乙酸是 HOOC–CO–CH₂–COOH：四个碳，两个羧基加一个酮基。「CHR」应是 CH₂（也可能是把 CH2 听成了 CHR）。那个酮基不是可有可无的细节——正是它让草酰乙酸能被还原成苹果酸（羟基）或转氨成天冬氨酸（氨基），这两条正是它出线粒体的方式。
extra.en: He dictates oxaloacetate as COOH / CHR / COOH and leaves out the keto carbon. Oxaloacetate is HOOC-CO-CH2-COOH: four carbons, two carboxyls and one keto group. The 'CHR' should be CH2 (possibly a mishearing of CH2). That keto group is not an optional detail: it is precisely what lets oxaloacetate be reduced to malate (hydroxyl) or transaminated to aspartate (amino), which are exactly the two ways it leaves the mitochondrion.

extra.zh: 他说 F6P → 1,6-二磷酸果糖 的 ΔG「稍微偏正、是吸能的」，用这个理由解释逆反应为何不耗能。结论对（果糖二磷酸酶水解磷酸酯键是放能的，不需要 ATP），但前提说反了：PFK-1 催化的整体反应把 ATP 水解偶联进来，ΔG°′ ≈ −14 kJ/mol，是强放能、生理上不可逆的。只有把 ATP 拆开、单看「F6P + Pi → F1,6BP」这半步才是吸能的（约 +16 kJ/mol）。按他的说法记，会误以为糖酵解的 PFK 那一步是吸能步骤。
extra.en: He calls the delta G of F6P to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate 'slightly positive, endergonic', using that to explain why the reverse costs nothing. The conclusion is right (FBPase hydrolyses a phosphate ester and is exergonic, needing no ATP) but the premise is inverted: the overall PFK-1 reaction has ATP hydrolysis coupled in, with a delta G of about -14 kJ/mol, strongly exergonic and physiologically irreversible. Only the half-reaction F6P + Pi to F1,6BP, with the ATP taken out, is endergonic at about +16 kJ/mol. Taking his version literally would make the PFK step of glycolysis look endergonic.

extra.zh: 他在讲最后一步时随口把 G6P 叫成「6-磷酸果糖」，同一句里又正确地说「G6P 转变为葡萄糖」。糖异生最后一步是葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶把 G6P 水解成葡萄糖，酶位于内质网腔面，产物再经转运体送出细胞——这就是为什么只有肝、肾和肠上皮能升血糖。F6P 是它前一步的化合物，两者由磷酸葡萄糖异构酶互变。
extra.en: While covering the last step he slips and calls G6P 'fructose-6-phosphate', then within the same sentence says correctly that G6P becomes glucose. The final step is glucose-6-phosphatase hydrolysing G6P to glucose, with the enzyme facing the ER lumen and the product exported by transporters, which is why only liver, kidney and intestinal epithelium can raise blood glucose. F6P is the compound one step earlier, interconverted with G6P by phosphoglucose isomerase.

quiz.q_zh: 丙酮酸变成磷酸烯醇丙酮酸的两步，酶和区室分别是什么？
quiz.q_en: Which enzymes and compartments carry pyruvate to phosphoenolpyruvate?

options.zh: 丙酮酸脱氢酶在细胞质，羧化酶在线粒体外膜
options.en: Pyruvate dehydrogenase in cytosol, carboxylase outside

options.zh: 丙酮酸羧化酶在线粒体基质，PEPCK 在胞浆中
options.en: Pyruvate carboxylase in the matrix, then PEPCK in cytosol

options.zh: 丙酮酸羧化酶在胞质，PEPCK 在线粒体基质
options.en: Pyruvate carboxylase in the cytosol, then PEPCK in matrix

options.zh: 丙酮酸激酶在线粒体基质，PEPCK 在内膜上
options.en: Pyruvate kinase in the matrix, PEPCK on inner membrane

quiz.explain_zh: 丙酮酸羧化酶在线粒体基质（生物素辅基、耗 ATP、乙酰CoA 别构激活），草酰乙酸以苹果酸或天冬氨酸形式出线粒体后，由胞质的 PEPCK 耗 GTP 生成 PEP。他一开始把区室说反了，约 18:05 自己纠正过来。丙酮酸激酶催化的是正向那一步，丙酮酸脱氢酶把丙酮酸变成乙酰CoA，都不在这条路线上。
quiz.explain_en: Pyruvate carboxylase sits in the mitochondrial matrix (biotin cofactor, ATP-consuming, allosterically activated by acetyl-CoA), and after oxaloacetate leaves as malate or aspartate, cytosolic PEPCK spends GTP to make PEP. He states the compartments backwards at first and corrects himself around 18:05. Pyruvate kinase catalyses the forward step and pyruvate dehydrogenase makes acetyl-CoA, neither of which is on this route.

quiz.q_zh: 草酰乙酸的结构是下面哪一个？
quiz.q_en: Which structure is oxaloacetate?

options.zh: HOOC–CO–CH₂–COOH，四碳，一个酮基两个羧基
options.en: HOOC-CO-CH2-COOH, four carbons, one keto, two carboxyls

options.zh: HOOC–CHOH–CH₂–COOH，四碳，一个羟基两个羧基
options.en: HOOC-CHOH-CH2-COOH, four carbons, hydroxyl and carboxyls

options.zh: HOOC–CH₂–COOH，三碳，一个亚甲基连两个羧基
options.en: HOOC-CH2-COOH, three carbons, methylene and two carboxyls

options.zh: HOOC–CH₂–CH₂–COOH，四碳，没有酮基只有羧基
options.en: HOOC-CH2-CH2-COOH, four carbons, two carboxyls, no keto

quiz.explain_zh: 草酰乙酸是 HOOC–CO–CH₂–COOH，四碳，含一个酮基和两个羧基；课上口述只报了三个基团，漏掉了酮基碳。只有羧基没有酮基的四碳二羧酸是琥珀酸，带羟基的是苹果酸，三碳的二羧酸是丙二酸。正是那个酮基让草酰乙酸能被还原成苹果酸或转氨成天冬氨酸而离开线粒体。
quiz.explain_en: Oxaloacetate is HOOC-CO-CH2-COOH: four carbons with one keto group and two carboxyls, whereas the dictated version lists only three groups and drops the keto carbon. The four-carbon diacid with no keto group is succinate, the one with a hydroxyl is malate, and the three-carbon diacid is malonate. That keto group is exactly what lets oxaloacetate be reduced to malate or transaminated to aspartate in order to leave the mitochondrion.

quiz.q_zh: 关于 F6P → 1,6-二磷酸果糖 这一步的能量学，正确的说法是？
quiz.q_en: Which statement about the energetics of F6P to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is correct?

options.zh: PFK-1 催化的正反应 ΔG°′ 稍微偏正，是一个吸能的步骤
options.en: The PFK-1 forward reaction is slightly positive, so endergonic

options.zh: PFK-1 催化的正反应不涉及 ATP，靠底物浓度推动进行
options.en: The PFK-1 forward reaction uses no ATP and is substrate-driven

options.zh: PFK-1 催化的正反应放能很小，正反两方向都很容易发生
options.en: The PFK-1 forward reaction is barely exergonic, running both ways

options.zh: PFK-1 催化的正反应偶联 ATP 水解，整体强放能不可逆
options.en: The PFK-1 forward reaction couples ATP hydrolysis, irreversible

quiz.explain_zh: PFK-1 把 ATP 水解偶联进来，整体 ΔG°′ ≈ −14 kJ/mol，强放能、生理不可逆——这正是糖异生必须另找果糖二磷酸酶绕过它的原因。课上说这一步 ΔG 稍偏正、是吸能的，把前提说反了；只有把 ATP 拆开单看 F6P + Pi → F1,6BP 才是吸能的（约 +16 kJ/mol）。说它不涉及 ATP 或两个方向都容易发生，也与它作为不可逆调控节点的地位矛盾。
quiz.explain_en: PFK-1 couples ATP hydrolysis into the reaction, giving an overall delta G of about -14 kJ/mol, strongly exergonic and physiologically irreversible, which is exactly why gluconeogenesis needs fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase to get around it. The lecture inverts the premise by calling it slightly positive and endergonic; only the ATP-free half-reaction F6P + Pi to F1,6BP is endergonic, at about +16 kJ/mol. Saying it uses no ATP, or that it runs easily both ways, also contradicts its status as an irreversible regulatory node.

title_zh: 糖异生的能量代价、调节与在饥饿中的位置
title_en: The energy cost of gluconeogenesis, its regulation, and its place in fasting

points.zh: 总结：糖异生就是克服了 EMP 途径的三个不可逆反应，由丙酮酸重新生成葡萄糖的过程。
points.en: Summary: gluconeogenesis is the process of remaking glucose from pyruvate by getting past the three irreversible reactions of EMP.

points.zh: 需要稍微记一下的数字：两分子丙酮酸生成一分子葡萄糖，消耗四分子 ATP 加两分子 GTP。
points.en: One number worth remembering: making one glucose from two pyruvate costs four ATP plus two GTP.

points.zh: 他特别指出 GTP 这一项比较特殊，要记住是 4 ATP + 2 GTP。
points.en: He notes that the GTP term is the unusual part, and to remember it as 4 ATP plus 2 GTP.

points.zh: 糖异生的调节完全不用看，因为学完糖这一章，闭着眼睛也能答出来。
points.en: The regulation of gluconeogenesis need not be studied, since after finishing the carbohydrate chapter one can answer it blind.

points.zh: 他的推理：糖异生被抑制，说明机体不缺葡萄糖；葡萄糖多就会产生大量 ATP，ATP 多的情况下糖异生就被抑制。
points.en: His reasoning: if gluconeogenesis is inhibited the body is not short of glucose; plenty of glucose means plenty of ATP, and with ATP high gluconeogenesis is inhibited.

points.zh: 他说这是很感性就能说出来的答案，所以「什么酶的调节」那些内容都不用看。
points.en: He calls this an answer one can give intuitively, so the enzyme-by-enzyme regulation material can all be skipped.

points.zh: 糖异生的意义：在饥饿状态下维持血糖稳定。
points.en: The significance of gluconeogenesis: keeping blood glucose stable during fasting.

points.zh: 他举 16+8 饮食法为例：8 小时内完成一天进食，其余 16 小时不吃；在血糖消耗完以后就会开始糖异生。
points.en: He cites 16:8 intermittent fasting: all eating within an 8-hour window and none for the other 16; once blood glucose is spent, gluconeogenesis starts.

points.zh: 他说机体最直接的能量来源还是葡萄糖，葡萄糖消耗完了糖异生也没办法再进行，丙酮酸也消耗得差不多了，最终才转向用脂肪供能，所以糖异生排在脂肪前面。
points.en: He says glucose remains the body's most direct energy source, that once glucose is spent gluconeogenesis can no longer proceed and pyruvate is largely used up as well, so the body finally turns to fat, placing gluconeogenesis ahead of fat.

extra.zh: 「葡萄糖消耗完了糖异生也没办法再进行」把因果说反了。糖异生的底物是乳酸、甘油和生糖氨基酸，不是葡萄糖；血糖耗尽恰恰是糖异生开动的条件，不是它停止的条件。他随后改口说是丙酮酸耗尽，方向对了一些，但真正的限制是生糖前体（尤其是肌肉蛋白分解出的丙氨酸和谷氨酰胺）的供应。
extra.en: 'Once glucose is used up gluconeogenesis can no longer run' inverts cause and effect. Its substrates are lactate, glycerol and glucogenic amino acids, not glucose; an exhausted blood glucose is precisely the trigger for gluconeogenesis, not the reason it stops. He then revises this to pyruvate running out, which is closer, but the real limit is the supply of glucogenic precursors, above all alanine and glutamine released by muscle protein breakdown.

extra.zh: 「糖异生排在脂肪前面」过度简化了。禁食时的顺序是肝糖原分解（数小时内耗尽）→ 糖异生成为主力，而脂肪动员几乎同时就开始了：脂肪酸 β-氧化产生的 ATP 和 NADH 正是肝脏跑糖异生的能量来源，甘油三酯水解出的甘油还直接充当糖异生底物。两者是并行、互相支撑的，不是先后接力。
extra.en: 'Gluconeogenesis comes before fat' oversimplifies. In fasting the order is glycogenolysis (exhausted within hours), then gluconeogenesis as the main supplier, but fat mobilisation begins almost simultaneously: the ATP and NADH from fatty acid beta-oxidation are exactly what powers hepatic gluconeogenesis, and the glycerol released by triglyceride hydrolysis is itself a gluconeogenic substrate. The two run in parallel and support each other rather than taking turns.

extra.zh: 4 ATP + 2 GTP 的账要配上 2 个 NADH 才完整：2 丙酮酸 + 4 ATP + 2 GTP + 2 NADH + 2 H⁺ + 4 H₂O → 1 葡萄糖 + 4 ADP + 2 GDP + 6 Pi + 2 NAD⁺。糖酵解正向只净得 2 ATP，糖异生却要花 6 个高能磷酸键，多出来的 4 个就是买下「不可逆」这三个绕行步骤的代价。
extra.en: The 4 ATP plus 2 GTP ledger is only complete with 2 NADH: 2 pyruvate + 4 ATP + 2 GTP + 2 NADH + 2 H+ + 4 H2O gives 1 glucose + 4 ADP + 2 GDP + 6 Pi + 2 NAD+. Glycolysis nets only 2 ATP going forward while gluconeogenesis spends six high-energy phosphate bonds; the extra four are the price of the three irreversible bypasses.

extra.zh: 他说调节「不用看」，但真正的考点是能量分子之外的那几个别构与激素信号：乙酰CoA 别构激活丙酮酸羧化酶（脂肪氧化旺盛时自动把丙酮酸推向糖异生），果糖-2,6-二磷酸抑制 FBPase-1 并激活 PFK-1（胰高血糖素经 cAMP-PKA 降低 F-2,6-BP，从而开糖异生、关糖酵解），皮质醇诱导 PEPCK 的转录。答「ATP 多就抑制」方向不错，但答不到点上。
extra.en: He says regulation can be skipped, but the examinable content is the allosteric and hormonal signals rather than ATP itself: acetyl-CoA allosterically activates pyruvate carboxylase (so brisk fat oxidation automatically pushes pyruvate towards gluconeogenesis), fructose-2,6-bisphosphate inhibits FBPase-1 while activating PFK-1 (glucagon lowers F-2,6-BP through cAMP and PKA, thereby switching gluconeogenesis on and glycolysis off), and cortisol induces transcription of PEPCK. 'High ATP inhibits it' has the right direction but misses the mechanism.

quiz.q_zh: 两分子丙酮酸生成一分子葡萄糖，他要求记住的能量代价是多少？
quiz.q_en: What energy cost for making one glucose from two pyruvate does he ask to be remembered?

options.zh: 两分子 ATP 加两分子 GTP
options.en: Two molecules of ATP plus two of GTP

options.zh: 六分子 ATP，不消耗 GTP
options.en: Six molecules of ATP and no GTP at all

options.zh: 两分子 ATP 加两分子 NADH
options.en: Two molecules of ATP plus two of NADH

options.zh: 四分子 ATP 加两分子 GTP
options.en: Four molecules of ATP plus two of GTP

quiz.explain_zh: 他强调「四分子 ATP 加两分子 GTP，这个 GTP 比较特殊，稍微记一下」。完整的账里还有 2 个 NADH（3-磷酸甘油醛脱氢酶那一步的逆向），但只写 ATP+NADH 或只写 ATP 都对不上他给的数字，合计六个高能磷酸键不能全算成 ATP。
quiz.explain_en: He stresses four ATP plus two GTP, with the GTP as the unusual item to note. The complete ledger also includes 2 NADH (the reverse of the glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase step), but writing only ATP plus NADH, or only ATP, does not match his figure, and the six high-energy phosphate bonds cannot all be counted as ATP.

quiz.q_zh: 长时间禁食时，糖异生的底物主要是什么？
quiz.q_en: During prolonged fasting, what are the main substrates for gluconeogenesis?

options.zh: 血中剩余的游离葡萄糖
options.en: The free glucose still left in the blood

options.zh: 乳酸、甘油和生糖氨基酸
options.en: Lactate, glycerol and glucogenic amino acids

options.zh: 线粒体里的乙酰CoA
options.en: Acetyl-CoA arriving from the mitochondria

options.zh: 肠道吸收来的膳食果糖
options.en: Dietary fructose absorbed from the intestine

quiz.explain_zh: 底物是乳酸（Cori 循环）、甘油（脂肪水解）和生糖氨基酸（主要是丙氨酸、谷氨酰胺）。课上说「葡萄糖消耗完糖异生也没办法进行」，方向说反了——血糖耗尽正是它开动的条件。乙酰CoA 在人体内不能净生成葡萄糖（丙酮酸脱氢酶那一步不可逆）；禁食时也没有膳食果糖可吸收。
quiz.explain_en: The substrates are lactate (the Cori cycle), glycerol (from fat hydrolysis) and glucogenic amino acids, chiefly alanine and glutamine. The lecture's claim that gluconeogenesis stops once glucose runs out is backwards, since exhausted blood glucose is exactly its trigger. Acetyl-CoA cannot give net glucose in humans because the pyruvate dehydrogenase step is irreversible, and during a fast there is no dietary fructose to absorb.

quiz.q_zh: 禁食过程中糖异生和脂肪动员的关系是怎样的？
quiz.q_en: How do gluconeogenesis and fat mobilisation relate during fasting?

options.zh: 两者互相排斥，同一时间只能跑一条
options.en: They exclude each other, so only one route runs at a time

options.zh: 先跑完糖异生，脂肪动员这才开始启动
options.en: Gluconeogenesis finishes first, then fat mobilisation begins

options.zh: 脂肪动员先启动，糖异生要等到最后才开动
options.en: Fat mobilisation starts first and gluconeogenesis comes last

options.zh: 两者几乎同时进行，脂肪酸供能给糖异生
options.en: Both run together, with fatty acids powering gluconeogenesis

quiz.explain_zh: 脂肪动员几乎与糖异生同时开始：β-氧化产生的 ATP 和 NADH 正是肝脏跑糖异生的能量来源，甘油三酯水解出的甘油还直接作糖异生底物，乙酰CoA 又别构激活丙酮酸羧化酶。课上说的「糖异生排在脂肪前面」是接力式的简化；说脂肪先、糖异生最后同样不对（肝糖原分解才是第一位的）；两者也不互相排斥。
quiz.explain_en: Fat mobilisation begins essentially alongside gluconeogenesis: the ATP and NADH from beta-oxidation power hepatic gluconeogenesis, the glycerol from triglyceride hydrolysis is itself a substrate, and acetyl-CoA allosterically activates pyruvate carboxylase. The lecture's relay picture of gluconeogenesis before fat is a simplification; putting fat first and gluconeogenesis last is equally wrong, since glycogenolysis comes first; and the two are not mutually exclusive.

title_zh: 乳酸循环 (Cori cycle)：肌肉产乳酸、肝脏还糖
title_en: The Cori cycle: muscle makes lactate, liver gives back glucose

points.zh: 乳酸循环的英文名是 Cori 循环，老师把它当作糖异生这一节后面的一个小知识点提出来。
points.en: The lactate cycle is called the Cori cycle; he introduces it as a small add-on to the gluconeogenesis section.

points.zh: 触发场景是突然的剧烈无氧运动：肌肉细胞里发生大量糖酵解 (EMP)。
points.en: The trigger is sudden strenuous anaerobic exercise: massive glycolysis (EMP) runs in muscle cells.

points.zh: 糖酵解的终产物是丙酮酸，他重复强调了两遍，所以丙酮酸会在肌肉细胞里大量积累。
points.en: The end product of glycolysis is pyruvate — he repeats this twice — so pyruvate piles up inside the muscle cell.

points.zh: 他说肌肉细胞不是 TCA 循环的主要场所，因为 TCA 要靠大量氧气才能把丙酮酸彻底分解，而运动中的肌肉通常拿不到足够的氧。
points.en: He says muscle is not the main site of the TCA cycle, because the TCA cycle needs plenty of oxygen to finish oxidising pyruvate, and working muscle does not get it.

points.zh: 他给乳酸循环的功能定义是：把丙酮酸送到真正有氧、能大量跑 TCA 的地方消耗掉，别让它堆在肌肉里。
points.en: His functional definition: ship the pyruvate to a place that really is aerobic and runs the TCA cycle, so it stops accumulating in muscle.

points.zh: 第一步：丙酮酸 (他板书写作 PA) 在乳酸脱氢酶的作用下加上两个氢，变成乳酸。
points.en: Step one: pyruvate (he writes PA) takes on two hydrogens under lactate dehydrogenase and becomes lactate.

points.zh: 他说这一步的还原力来自磷酸戊糖途径，并说「NADPH 或者叫 NADH 都可以」，理由是 EMP 活跃的细胞（尤其肌肉）里 PPP 也活跃。
points.en: He says the reducing power for this step comes from the pentose phosphate pathway and that "NADPH or NADH, either name works", reasoning that PPP is active wherever EMP is active, especially in muscle.

points.zh: 乳酸靠一些特殊的蛋白被带到肝脏；肝里大量的乳酸脱氢酶又把氢重新拿走，乳酸变回丙酮酸。
points.en: Lactate is carried to the liver by specific proteins; the abundant liver lactate dehydrogenase pulls the hydrogens back off and regenerates pyruvate.

points.zh: 肝内丙酮酸有两条去路：一是直接进 TCA 循环彻底分解产能，二是经糖异生变成葡萄糖，葡萄糖入血后很快被肌肉细胞摄取，循环闭合。
points.en: Liver pyruvate has two fates: straight into the TCA cycle to be burned, or through gluconeogenesis to glucose, which enters the blood and is rapidly taken up by muscle, closing the loop.

extra.zh: 他说乳酸脱氢酶用的 NADH 来自磷酸戊糖途径，并三次说「NADPH 或者叫 NADH 都可以」，全程没有收回。实际上磷酸戊糖途径产的是 NADPH，只用于还原性生物合成（脂肪酸、胆固醇）和维持谷胱甘肽还原态；乳酸脱氢酶用的是糖酵解 GAPDH 那一步产生的 NADH。NADPH 比 NADH 多一个 2′-磷酸，就是酶识别的标签，两者不能互称也不能直接互换。
extra.en: He says the NADH used by lactate dehydrogenase comes from the pentose phosphate pathway, and three times says "NADPH or NADH, either is fine", never retracting it. The PPP makes NADPH, which serves reductive biosynthesis (fatty acids, cholesterol) and keeps glutathione reduced. LDH uses the NADH generated at the GAPDH step of glycolysis. The extra 2′-phosphate on NADPH is exactly the tag enzymes read; the two are neither interchangeable names nor interchangeable substrates.

extra.zh: 为什么非得做乳酸？无氧时糖酵解每消耗一分子葡萄糖要在 GAPDH 那一步用掉 2 个 NAD⁺；细胞里 NAD⁺ 总量很小，如果不把 NADH 重新氧化回 NAD⁺，糖酵解就会卡死在 GAPDH。丙酮酸→乳酸就是这个再生反应，乳酸本身是「废渣」，NAD⁺ 才是目的。老师讲的是「把丙酮酸运走」，这只是结果的一半。
extra.en: Why lactate at all? Anaerobic glycolysis consumes 2 NAD+ per glucose at the GAPDH step, and the cell's total NAD pool is tiny — without reoxidising NADH back to NAD+, glycolysis stalls at GAPDH. Pyruvate to lactate is that regeneration reaction; lactate is the waste, NAD+ is the point. "Getting rid of pyruvate", as taught, is only half the story.

extra.zh: Cori cycle 整体是净耗能的：肌肉端每分子葡萄糖净得 2 ATP，肝脏端由乳酸重新造一分子葡萄糖要花 6 个高能磷酸键（4 ATP + 2 GTP），一圈净亏 4 个。它的意义不是省能量，而是把能量负担从缺氧的肌肉转移到有氧的肝脏。
extra.en: The Cori cycle costs energy overall: the muscle end nets 2 ATP per glucose, while the liver end spends 6 high-energy phosphates (4 ATP + 2 GTP) to rebuild one glucose — a net loss of 4 per turn. Its point is not efficiency but shifting the energetic burden from oxygen-starved muscle to the aerobic liver.

extra.zh: 他说循环是「把丙酮酸运输到有氧的地方」。实际离开肌肉进血的是乳酸，不是丙酮酸——乳酸由 MCT（单羧酸转运体）跨膜。另外肝里「重新拿走氢」的不是另一种酶，仍是乳酸脱氢酶，只是同工酶组成不同（心肌/肝偏 H 型，骨骼肌偏 M 型），反应方向由 NADH/NAD⁺ 比和底物浓度决定，这个酶本身是可逆的。
extra.en: He describes the cycle as "transporting pyruvate to an aerobic site". What actually leaves muscle for the blood is lactate, moved by MCT monocarboxylate transporters. And the liver enzyme that "takes the hydrogens back" is still lactate dehydrogenase, just a different isozyme mix (H-type in heart/liver, M-type in skeletal muscle); the enzyme is freely reversible and direction is set by the NADH/NAD+ ratio and substrate levels.

quiz.q_zh: 乳酸脱氢酶把丙酮酸还原成乳酸时，所用的还原力真正来自哪里？
quiz.q_en: Where does the reducing power actually come from when lactate dehydrogenase reduces pyruvate to lactate?

options.zh: 磷酸戊糖途径氧化阶段产生的 NADPH
options.en: NADPH from the oxidative phase of the PPP

options.zh: 线粒体基质里 TCA 循环的 NADH
options.en: NADH from the TCA cycle in the matrix

options.zh: 苹果酸-天冬氨酸穿梭送入的 NADH
options.en: NADH delivered by the malate-aspartate shuttle

options.zh: 糖酵解 GAPDH 步骤产生的 NADH
options.en: NADH made at the GAPDH step of glycolysis

quiz.explain_zh: 糖酵解 GAPDH 那一步把 NAD⁺ 还原成 NADH，乳酸脱氢酶正是把这份 NADH 重新氧化回 NAD⁺，糖酵解才能继续。磷酸戊糖途径的 NADPH 只供还原性合成和抗氧化，酶靠 2′-磷酸区分二者；TCA 的 NADH 在线粒体基质内直接交给呼吸链，不出线粒体；苹果酸-天冬氨酸穿梭是把胞浆还原当量送进线粒体，方向正好相反。
quiz.explain_en: The GAPDH step reduces NAD+ to NADH, and LDH reoxidises exactly that NADH so glycolysis can keep running. PPP NADPH serves reductive synthesis and antioxidant defence and is distinguished by its 2′-phosphate; TCA NADH stays in the matrix and feeds the respiratory chain; the malate-aspartate shuttle moves cytosolic reducing equivalents inward, the opposite direction.

quiz.q_zh: 无氧条件下肌肉必须把丙酮酸变成乳酸，最根本的原因是什么？
quiz.q_en: What is the fundamental reason anaerobic muscle must convert pyruvate to lactate?

options.zh: 为了让肌肉细胞额外多产出两分子 ATP
options.en: To give the muscle cell two extra molecules of ATP

options.zh: 为了把丙酮酸转成 TCA 循环可用的底物
options.en: To turn pyruvate into a substrate the TCA can use

options.zh: 为了把 NADH 氧化回 NAD⁺ 维持糖酵解
options.en: To reoxidise NADH to NAD+ and sustain glycolysis

options.zh: 为了阻止丙酮酸生成乙酰CoA 进入线粒体
options.en: To stop pyruvate forming acetyl-CoA in mitochondria

quiz.explain_zh: 细胞内 NAD⁺ 总量很小，GAPDH 每轮都要消耗 NAD⁺，不把 NADH 氧化回来糖酵解就停摆。乳酸这一步本身不产 ATP，所以「多产出两分子 ATP」不成立；乳酸不是 TCA 的底物，进 TCA 的是乙酰CoA；也没有「阻止丙酮酸进线粒体」这回事，缺氧时线粒体本来就跑不动。
quiz.explain_en: The NAD+ pool is small and GAPDH consumes it every round, so glycolysis halts unless NADH is reoxidised. The lactate step itself makes no ATP, so "two extra ATP" is wrong; lactate is not a TCA substrate — acetyl-CoA is; and nothing is "blocking" pyruvate entry, since without oxygen the mitochondria cannot run anyway.

quiz.q_zh: Cori 循环由哪两条途径在哪两个器官里配对组成？
quiz.q_en: Which two pathways, in which two organs, make up the Cori cycle?

options.zh: 肌肉糖酵解 + 肝脏糖异生
options.en: Muscle glycolysis + gluconeogenesis in the liver

options.zh: 肝脏糖酵解 + 肌肉三羧酸循环
options.en: Liver glycolysis + the citric acid cycle in muscle

options.zh: 肌肉糖异生 + 肝脏磷酸戊糖途径
options.en: Muscle gluconeogenesis + liver pentose phosphate route

options.zh: 肌肉磷酸戊糖途径 + 肝脏糖异生
options.en: Muscle pentose phosphate route + liver gluconeogenesis

quiz.explain_zh: 肌肉无氧糖酵解产乳酸，乳酸入血到肝，肝用糖异生把它变回葡萄糖再送出去。磷酸戊糖途径不参与这个循环（老师在 41:20 附近把它配了进去，是错的）；肌肉几乎没有葡萄糖-6-磷酸酶，不能做糖异生；肝脏在这个场景里做的是糖异生而不是糖酵解，TCA 也不是循环的组成环节。
quiz.explain_en: Anaerobic muscle glycolysis makes lactate, the blood carries it to the liver, and hepatic gluconeogenesis rebuilds glucose and exports it. The PPP is not part of this loop (he pairs it in around 41:20, which is wrong); muscle essentially lacks glucose-6-phosphatase and cannot do gluconeogenesis; the liver here runs gluconeogenesis, not glycolysis, and the TCA cycle is not a limb of the cycle.

title_zh: 乙醛酸循环：植物和微生物给 TCA 抄的近路
title_en: The glyoxylate cycle: the shortcut plants and microbes take through the TCA cycle

points.zh: 他说乙醛酸循环是个小知识点，但很爱考，尤其医学类的考试和考研，他自己当年考研就考到过。
points.en: He flags the glyoxylate cycle as a small point that gets examined a lot, especially in medical and graduate entrance exams — he was asked about it himself.

points.zh: 这条循环只在植物和微生物里进行，人体内完全没有。
points.en: The cycle runs only in plants and microorganisms; it does not exist in humans at all.

points.zh: 原因是只有植物和微生物才有两种酶：异柠檬酸裂解酶和苹果酸合酶。
points.en: The reason is that only plants and microbes have two enzymes: isocitrate lyase and malate synthase.

points.zh: 他形容这两个酶「把 TCA 循环给截胡了」。
points.en: He describes the two enzymes as "hijacking" the TCA cycle.

points.zh: 正常 TCA 里异柠檬酸要走很长一段才到琥珀酸、琥珀酰CoA 等等；乙醛酸循环里异柠檬酸直接裂解成乙醛酸。
points.en: In the normal TCA cycle isocitrate takes a long route to succinate and succinyl-CoA; in the glyoxylate cycle isocitrate is cleaved straight to glyoxylate.

points.zh: 乙醛酸接受一分子乙酰CoA 就变成苹果酸（苹果酸合酶那一步）。
points.en: Glyoxylate takes on one acetyl-CoA to become malate — the malate synthase step.

points.zh: 苹果酸再直接变成草酰乙酸，等于把 TCA 循环图下半部分一大半全砍掉了。
points.en: Malate then goes straight to oxaloacetate, cutting away most of the lower half of the TCA diagram.

points.zh: 他说这样从 11 步还是 12 步的反应直接变成 4 步的反应。
points.en: He says this turns an 11- or 12-step sequence into a 4-step one.

points.zh: 结论：草酰乙酸可以掺入糖异生途径，所以植物和微生物能由乙酰CoA 进行糖异生，人不行。
points.en: Conclusion: oxaloacetate can feed gluconeogenesis, so plants and microbes can make sugar from acetyl-CoA while humans cannot.

extra.zh: 他说异柠檬酸「下一步是产生琥珀酸」，跳掉了一个节点。真实顺序是 异柠檬酸 →（异柠檬酸脱氢酶，放 CO₂ + NADH）α-酮戊二酸 →（α-酮戊二酸脱氢酶复合体）琥珀酰CoA → 琥珀酸。被跳掉的 α-酮戊二酸恰恰是本课后半段氨基酸代谢最重要的接口（谷氨酸 ↔ α-酮戊二酸的转氨基）。
extra.en: He says isocitrate's "next step is to produce succinate", skipping a node. The real order is isocitrate → (isocitrate dehydrogenase, releasing CO2 + NADH) α-ketoglutarate → (α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex) succinyl-CoA → succinate. The α-ketoglutarate he skips is precisely the interface with amino acid metabolism later in this lecture (glutamate ↔ α-ketoglutarate transamination).

extra.zh: 异柠檬酸裂解酶的产物他只说了乙醛酸，漏了琥珀酸。实际是 异柠檬酸 → 乙醛酸 + 琥珀酸，而漏掉的琥珀酸才是净流出的四碳骨架（琥珀酸 → 延胡索酸 → 苹果酸 → 草酰乙酸 → 糖异生）。另外整圈要消耗两分子乙酰CoA（柠檬酸合酶一分子、苹果酸合酶一分子），他只提了苹果酸合酶那一分子。
extra.en: He names only glyoxylate as the isocitrate lyase product and omits succinate. The reaction is isocitrate → glyoxylate + succinate, and the missing succinate is the four-carbon skeleton that actually leaves (succinate → fumarate → malate → oxaloacetate → gluconeogenesis). The full turn also consumes two acetyl-CoA — one at citrate synthase, one at malate synthase — where he mentions only the malate synthase one.

extra.zh: 「11 步或 12 步变成 4 步」是随口说的。三羧酸循环是 8 步，乙醛酸循环是 5 步，其中 3 步与 TCA 共用（柠檬酸合酶、乌头酸酶、苹果酸脱氢酶），另 2 步是那两个专属酶。真正被绕开的是两个脱羧步骤（异柠檬酸脱氢酶和 α-酮戊二酸脱氢酶），这才是碳骨架不被烧成 CO₂ 的原因。
extra.en: The "11 or 12 steps down to 4" is off the cuff. The TCA cycle is 8 steps; the glyoxylate cycle is 5, three of them shared with the TCA cycle (citrate synthase, aconitase, malate dehydrogenase) plus the two unique enzymes. What is actually bypassed are the two decarboxylations — isocitrate dehydrogenase and the α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex — and that is why the carbon skeleton is not burned off as CO2.

extra.zh: 定位没讲：在植物里这条循环发生在一种专门的细胞器——乙醛酸循环体 (glyoxysome)，属于过氧化物酶体家族，油料种子萌发时大量出现；脂肪酸在同一细胞器里 β-氧化产生乙酰CoA，就地进入循环。琥珀酸再出去进线粒体转成苹果酸，苹果酸到胞质氧化成草酰乙酸后进糖异生。
extra.en: Localisation was not covered: in plants this cycle runs in a dedicated organelle, the glyoxysome, a member of the peroxisome family that proliferates when oily seeds germinate. Fatty acid β-oxidation in that same organelle supplies the acetyl-CoA on the spot. Succinate then exits to the mitochondrion to become malate, and cytosolic oxidation to oxaloacetate feeds gluconeogenesis.

quiz.q_zh: 乙醛酸循环只在植物和微生物中存在，直接原因是它们独有哪两种酶？
quiz.q_en: The glyoxylate cycle exists only in plants and microbes because they uniquely have which two enzymes?

options.zh: 苹果酸脱氢酶与延胡索酸水合酶
options.en: Malate dehydrogenase and fumarate hydratase

options.zh: 柠檬酸合酶与乌头酸水合酶
options.en: Citrate synthase and aconitate hydratase

options.zh: 丙酮酸羧化酶和 PEP 羧激酶
options.en: Pyruvate carboxylase and PEP carboxykinase

options.zh: 异柠檬酸裂解酶和苹果酸合酶
options.en: Isocitrate lyase and malate synthase

quiz.explain_zh: 异柠檬酸裂解酶把异柠檬酸切成乙醛酸 + 琥珀酸，苹果酸合酶让乙醛酸接上乙酰CoA 生成苹果酸，这两步绕开了两个脱羧反应。柠檬酸合酶、乌头酸酶、苹果酸脱氢酶都是与 TCA 共用的酶，人体同样具备；延胡索酸酶也是 TCA 常规酶；丙酮酸羧化酶和 PEPCK 属于糖异生，人体也有。
quiz.explain_en: Isocitrate lyase splits isocitrate into glyoxylate plus succinate, and malate synthase condenses glyoxylate with acetyl-CoA to malate, together bypassing the two decarboxylations. Citrate synthase, aconitase and malate dehydrogenase are shared TCA enzymes that humans also have; fumarase is likewise a standard TCA enzyme; pyruvate carboxylase and PEPCK belong to gluconeogenesis and exist in humans too.

quiz.q_zh: 乙醛酸循环之所以能让乙酰CoA 的碳最终变成糖，关键在于它绕过了什么？
quiz.q_en: The glyoxylate cycle lets acetyl-CoA carbon end up as sugar mainly because it bypasses what?

options.zh: 线粒体内膜上的电子传递与氧化磷酸化偶联
options.en: Electron transport coupled to oxidative phosphorylation

options.zh: 丙酮酸脱氢酶复合体产生乙酰CoA 那一步
options.en: The pyruvate dehydrogenase step that generates acetyl-CoA

options.zh: TCA 循环中两个放出 CO₂ 的脱羧步骤
options.en: The two CO2-releasing decarboxylation steps of the TCA cycle

options.zh: 糖酵解途径里三个不可逆的激酶催化步骤
options.en: The three irreversible kinase steps of the glycolytic pathway

quiz.explain_zh: 异柠檬酸脱氢酶和 α-酮戊二酸脱氢酶各放掉一个 CO₂，正是这两步让乙酰CoA 的两个碳在 TCA 里被烧光；跳过它们，四碳骨架就能净累积并进糖异生。糖酵解的不可逆步骤是糖异生自己要绕的，与本循环无关；电子传递链照常运行；丙酮酸脱氢酶那一步在这里根本不是入口，入口是脂肪酸 β-氧化来的乙酰CoA。
quiz.explain_en: Isocitrate dehydrogenase and the α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex each release a CO2, and those are the steps that burn off acetyl-CoA's two carbons in the TCA cycle; skipping them lets a four-carbon skeleton accumulate and enter gluconeogenesis. The irreversible glycolytic steps are what gluconeogenesis itself bypasses, unrelated here; the respiratory chain still runs; and pyruvate dehydrogenase is not the entry point — β-oxidation-derived acetyl-CoA is.

title_zh: 考研真题：种子里的油去哪了；人为什么不能把脂肪变成糖
title_en: An exam question about seed oil, and why humans cannot turn fat into glucose

points.zh: 他举了自己考研遇到的题：植物种子里富含大量油脂，为什么长成幼苗以后体内就不含这些油脂了。
points.en: He recalls an exam question he faced: seeds are rich in oil, so why does the grown seedling no longer contain it?

points.zh: 答案落在乙醛酸循环上：脂质分解的最终产物是乙酰CoA。
points.en: The answer turns on the glyoxylate cycle: the end product of lipid breakdown is acetyl-CoA.

points.zh: 人体不能用乙酰CoA 做糖异生，但植物可以。
points.en: Humans cannot run gluconeogenesis from acetyl-CoA, but plants can.

points.zh: 完整链条：种子油脂 → 分解代谢产生乙酰CoA → 乙醛酸循环 → 草酰乙酸 → 糖异生 → 糖类物质。
points.en: The full chain: seed oil → catabolism to acetyl-CoA → glyoxylate cycle → oxaloacetate → gluconeogenesis → carbohydrate.

points.zh: 这些糖被用来构筑植物身体，包括细胞壁的纤维素；他提醒纤维素也是一种糖，与淀粉不同。
points.en: That sugar builds the plant body, including cell-wall cellulose; he notes cellulose is also a sugar, different from starch.

points.zh: 很多微生物的细胞壁同样由多糖组成，所以乙醛酸循环让它们能高效地用脂质来建造身体。
points.en: Many microbial cell walls are polysaccharide too, so the glyoxylate cycle lets them build their bodies efficiently from lipid.

points.zh: 他强调「人不能拿脂肪变成葡萄糖」，并说这是一个很违背常识的点，值得花时间强调。
points.en: He stresses that humans cannot convert fat into glucose, calling it a counter-intuitive point worth dwelling on.

points.zh: 人体脂肪生成乙酰CoA 后只有一条路：草酰乙酸接受乙酰CoA 变成柠檬酸，进 TCA 循环被利用掉。
points.en: In humans, acetyl-CoA from fat has only one route: oxaloacetate takes it up as citrate and the TCA cycle disposes of it.

points.zh: 他补充丙酮酸也会变成乙酰CoA，走的是同一个入口。
points.en: He adds that pyruvate also becomes acetyl-CoA and enters by the same door.

extra.zh: 「人不能由脂肪造糖」的化学根据没讲：乙酰CoA 进 TCA 时是两个碳进去，异柠檬酸脱氢酶和 α-酮戊二酸脱氢酶又放掉两个 CO₂，净碳增加为零，所以草酰乙酸的量不会因为烧脂肪而变多。乙酰CoA → 丙酮酸这一步（丙酮酸脱氢酶复合体）在生理上不可逆，这是「单行道」的真正原因。
extra.en: The chemical basis of "humans cannot make sugar from fat" was left out: acetyl-CoA brings two carbons into the TCA cycle, and isocitrate dehydrogenase plus the α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex release two CO2, so net carbon gain is zero and burning fat never raises the oxaloacetate pool. The pyruvate dehydrogenase reaction is physiologically irreversible, and that one-way step is the real reason.

extra.zh: 脂肪不是完全不能变糖——甘油三酯的甘油骨架可以。甘油经甘油激酶生成 3-磷酸甘油，再氧化成磷酸二羟丙酮 (DHAP)，直接进糖异生。所以一分子甘油三酯里「不能变糖」的是三条脂肪酸链，能变糖的是那一个甘油。奇数碳脂肪酸最后剩下的丙酰CoA 同样可经琥珀酰CoA 生糖，只是量极少。
extra.en: Fat is not entirely sugar-proof — the glycerol backbone qualifies. Glycerol kinase makes glycerol-3-phosphate, oxidised to dihydroxyacetone phosphate, which enters gluconeogenesis directly. So within one triacylglycerol the three acyl chains cannot become sugar but the single glycerol can. Propionyl-CoA left over from odd-chain fatty acids likewise becomes glucose via succinyl-CoA, though the amounts are trivial.

extra.zh: 纤维素和淀粉的区别不只是「不一样的糖」：两者都是葡萄糖聚合物，差别在糖苷键构型——纤维素是 β-1,4，链呈伸直带状、相邻链间氢键成束；淀粉/糖原是 α-1,4，链呈螺旋。人体有 α-淀粉酶而没有纤维素酶，所以吃得下淀粉、消化不了纤维素。
extra.en: Cellulose and starch differ by more than being "different sugars": both are glucose polymers, and the difference is the glycosidic linkage. Cellulose is β-1,4, giving straight ribbon-like chains that hydrogen-bond into bundles; starch and glycogen are α-1,4 and coil into helices. Humans have α-amylase but no cellulase, which is why starch is food and cellulose is fibre.

extra.zh: 油料种子萌发这件事在实验上有名字：乙醛酸循环体只在萌发早期出现，几天后随着子叶转绿被过氧化物酶体取代（glyoxysome → peroxisome 转换）。这也解释了老师那道题的时间性——不是油「消失」了，是它在幼苗期被系统地改建成了细胞壁和可溶性糖。
extra.en: The germination phenomenon has a name in the literature: glyoxysomes appear only in early germination and are replaced by leaf peroxisomes within days as the cotyledons green (the glyoxysome-to-peroxisome transition). This explains the timing in his exam question — the oil does not vanish, it is systematically rebuilt into cell wall and soluble sugar during the seedling stage.

quiz.q_zh: 油料种子萌发时脂肪变成糖的正确顺序是什么？
quiz.q_en: In a germinating oilseed, what is the correct order by which fat becomes sugar?

options.zh: 脂肪酸 → 乙酰CoA → 乙醛酸循环 → 草酰乙酸 → 糖异生
options.en: Fatty acid to acetyl-CoA to glyoxylate cycle to oxaloacetate to sugar

options.zh: 脂肪酸 → 乙酰CoA → 酮体 → 磷酸戊糖途径 → 核酮糖
options.en: Fatty acid to acetyl-CoA to ketone bodies to the PPP to free ribulose

options.zh: 甘油 → 柠檬酸 → 异柠檬酸 → TCA 循环 → 游离葡萄糖
options.en: Glycerol to citrate to isocitrate to the TCA cycle to free glucose

options.zh: 脂肪酸 → 丙酮酸 → 乳酸 → 肝脏糖异生 → 游离葡萄糖
options.en: Fatty acid to pyruvate to lactate to liver gluconeogenesis to glucose

quiz.explain_zh: β-氧化把脂肪酸切成乙酰CoA，乙醛酸循环用异柠檬酸裂解酶和苹果酸合酶把两个乙酰单位变成四碳的草酰乙酸，草酰乙酸进糖异生。脂肪酸不能直接生成丙酮酸，因为丙酮酸脱氢酶那步不可逆；酮体是分解产物、且磷酸戊糖途径不由酮体启动；甘油确实能生糖，但它走 DHAP 进糖异生，不经柠檬酸和 TCA 循环。
quiz.explain_en: β-oxidation cuts fatty acids into acetyl-CoA; the glyoxylate cycle uses isocitrate lyase and malate synthase to turn two acetyl units into four-carbon oxaloacetate, which feeds gluconeogenesis.
